themes.name: other: unexpected_charge
themes.problem_statement: Statements about unexpected charge that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Overdraft fee although the shown balance covered it
themes.problem_statement: A customer is charged an overdraft, NSF or low-balance fee although the balance they could see covered the transaction.
themes.root_cause: Fees are assessed against the posted balance while pending items, late-posting deposits and delayed protection transfers leave the displayed available balance out of step.
examples: The customer was charged a $35 overdraft fee although he never overdrew his account, which the agent traced to a miscommunication in the bank's own system.
I was charged $35 for an overdraft even though I had more than enough money in my account, and it turned out to be a transaction processing issue.

themes.name: Flat overdraft fee per item, avoidable only by opting out
themes.problem_statement: Small shortfalls on everyday bills and purchases each draw a flat $30-$35 overdraft fee, and the fees pile up within a single month.
themes.root_cause: Overdraft coverage is on by default and priced per item rather than declining the transaction, so customers who dip below zero are charged repeatedly before they notice.
examples: I did not know what an overdraft fee was; it is $35 and the only way to avoid it altogether is to opt out and have transactions declined instead.
The $30 fee was an overdraft charge after the customer wrote a $500 check without realising his balance was low and went into the negative.

themes.name: Maintenance fee on a free account, and no waiver
themes.problem_statement: A maintenance or minimum-balance fee appears on an account the customer understood to be free, and the bank refuses to waive it.
themes.root_cause: The fee schedule and its waiver conditions (minimum balance, direct deposit) are not made clear at sign-up, so the customer first learns of them when the fee posts.
examples: XXXX insurance, tire/wheel coverage, and thousands of dollars in service fees were added to the loan without clear disclosure or the option to decline.
The customer was charged a fee because his checking balance fell below the $1500 minimum several times over the past few months, and he does not want it to keep happening.

themes.name: Unauthorised debits and subscriptions on the statement
themes.problem_statement: Debits, subscriptions or card purchases the customer does not recognise post to the account with no notice, and they must chase a refund.
themes.root_cause: Recurring debits and card-not-present purchases are accepted without a verified mandate and without any alert to the customer before the money leaves the account.
examples: Several small charges from different companies have come out of the account over the past few months, which the customer says she never gave permission for.
A $500 purchase from XYZ Inc. was charged on January 1st that I never made, for an order the cancellation email shows was cancelled on December 31st.

themes.name: Savings term broken early costs a withdrawal penalty
themes.problem_statement: Taking money out of a certificate of deposit before maturity costs a flat penalty or months of interest the customer says they were never told about.
themes.root_cause: The early withdrawal penalty is not surfaced when the term account is opened, so customers meet it only when an unexpected expense forces a withdrawal.
examples: The customer drew on her certificate of deposit to cover unexpected expenses and was charged an early withdrawal penalty, which she did not think fair for her own money.
The certificate of deposit carries a $250 penalty for withdrawing any part of the principal before maturity, which the customer thinks is steep.

themes.name: ATM, foreign and exchange fees just to use your own money
themes.problem_statement: Using an out-of-network ATM, a card abroad or a currency exchange adds a per-use fee on top of the amount the customer wanted, and it is never refunded.
themes.root_cause: Access-channel fees (out-of-network ATM, foreign transaction, conversion margin, branch surcharge) are priced per use and live only in the fee schedule, so customers meet them after the fact.
examples: I used my debit card abroad and was charged a foreign transaction fee on every purchase, which added up quickly, although I thought my international account covered that.
Buying 500 Euros would cost $595 including the 2% conversion fee, which the customer found a bit steep and asked how to avoid.

themes.name: Fee refund refused: the yearly courtesy limit is used up
themes.problem_statement: The bank accepts the fees are painful but will not reverse them, because the account has already used its annual or quarterly courtesy-refund allowance.
themes.root_cause: Fee reversals are capped per account per period by policy, so agents cannot address a run of fees once the quota is spent, however the fees arose.
examples: Multiple overdraft fees were charged on the same day the account first went negative, and Chase refused to reverse them beyond the one reversal allowed per year.
Thirteen overdraft fees totaling $440.00 were charged in one month, but representatives said a yearly reversal quota had already been met and only reversed $66.00 of the total.

themes.name: Refund or credit clawed back, overdrawing the account
themes.problem_statement: A refund, provisional credit or released deposit the bank had already given is pulled back later, pushing the account negative and leaving the customer owing the money.
themes.root_cause: Provisional credits and released deposits are reversed automatically when a claim closes or an item is returned, with no notice and no cover for the overdraft the reversal creates.
examples: After the unresolved fraud case, the bank is now demanding $1,700.00 be paid back.
Chase released the pending $700.00 deposit and let the scammer's $350.00 checks clear, and is now charging the customer the $700.00.

themes.name: Fees keep running on a closed or frozen account
themes.problem_statement: Fees and payments keep coming out of an account the customer has closed, cannot use or has had frozen, and the balance they are told they owe keeps growing.
themes.root_cause: Fee and payment processing follows the account record staying open in the system, so a freeze, a closure or dormancy does not stop the charges from being assessed.
examples: Over $60.00 a month in fees have accrued for the past year since the account was closed, adding up to $1200.00 the customer now owes and cannot afford.
A second monthly service fee posted before the first could be reversed, and the customer can't close the account because credit card payments are set to auto-debit from it through the banking app.

themes.name: The same fee or charge taken twice or at the wrong amount
themes.problem_statement: A fee or a purchase is taken twice, at the wrong amount, or with no transaction behind it at all, and the customer has to prove the bank's own mistake to get it back.
themes.root_cause: Fees and card charges post automatically at cycle or conversion time with no reconciliation against what was already taken, so duplicates surface only when a customer complains.
examples: The customer was charged random fees she did not understand; after she faxed a statement the bank found the fees were its own error and reversed them.
A $20 monthly maintenance fee was incorrectly charged as $40 due to a system error that charged the fee twice.

themes.name: Late fee although the payment was made on time
themes.problem_statement: A late fee and the interest behind it post although the customer paid before the due date or exactly on the plan the bank itself agreed.
themes.root_cause: Late fees are assessed on the posting date and the minimum-due cutoff rather than the date the customer paid, and agreed payment plans are not registered against the due date.
examples: A late fee was charged on the credit card and she was told she must either pay it or dispute the charge with evidence to get the fee and the negative mark removed.
A $34.00 interest charge was applied because $530.00 of the statement balance was paid one day after the minimum due date, even though it was paid two days before the statement cycle closed.

themes.name: Fees caused by a fraud or dispute are never reversed
themes.problem_statement: Overdraft, NSF, late and interest charges caused by a fraudulent or disputed transaction stay on the account even after the disputed amount itself is credited back.
themes.root_cause: A claim credits only the principal and leaves the fees the event generated outside the case, while billing keeps running on the disputed balance until the investigation closes.
examples: The bank withdrew several fees once the balance fell below the required amount due to the fraud withdrawals and never returned them.
While the scam was draining the account, Chase charged three overdraft fees and a minimum-balance fee totaling over $100.00, and refused to reimburse any of them.

themes.name: An everyday purchase billed as a cash advance
themes.problem_statement: A normal purchase is processed as a cash advance, adding a per-transaction fee and interest from day one that the customer cannot pay off on its own.
themes.root_cause: Merchant and platform coding decides the cash-advance classification at authorisation, with no warning at the time of purchase and no way to target a payment at that balance.
examples: A $92.00 charity purchase was charged a $10.00 cash-like transaction fee and coded as a cash advance subject to nearly 30% daily interest, with no way to pay off just that portion.
After forgetting to toggle the purchases tab on two payments, cash advance fees and interest were applied; the fees were refunded but the $18.00 interest was not.

themes.name: Interest higher than expected and a rate that will not move
themes.problem_statement: Interest keeps growing at a rate the customer did not expect, and the bank will not lower it, offering at most a one-time courtesy refund of the charges.
themes.root_cause: The APR is set by a risk model and repriced when a promotional period ends, so agents can credit charges back but cannot reduce the rate on the existing account.
examples: My APR is 22.99% on a $3,500 balance, which seems really high, and I was told it cannot be lowered because of my credit score and payment history.
The customer thinks her APR is high although she believes she has a good credit score, and asked how to dispute a charge or request a lower rate.

themes.name: Fee charged although a waiver or opt-out was agreed
themes.problem_statement: A fee lands although the customer opted out of overdraft, met the waiver condition, or was told the account, linkage or transfer would carry no such charge.
themes.root_cause: Waivers, account linkages, promotional exemptions and overdraft opt-outs are recorded on the customer request but never reach the system that assesses fees, so the charge posts anyway.
examples: Fee disclosures say a platinum business account linked to a private client account should have no wire transfer fees, but wires on the second linked business account are still being charged.
A $25.00 charge appeared on the checking account despite meeting the minimum combined balance requirement the entire time the account had been open.

themes.name: Annual fee kept and rewards lost when the card closes
themes.problem_statement: The annual or authorised-user fee is not refunded and earned rewards are forfeited when the card closes part-way through the year it paid for, often because the bank closed it.
themes.root_cause: Annual fees are billed a full year up front and closure runs as a separate process that neither prorates the fee already taken nor releases the rewards it paid for.
examples: Chase approved a United Airlines credit card with a high annual fee, then closed it a few months later without refunding the fee.
The customer asked for a prorated refund of the annual fee and compensation for the disruption caused by the sudden closure.

themes.name: Interest still charged after the balance was paid in full
themes.problem_statement: Interest still posts after the customer paid the statement balance in full and on time, at an amount never shown on the statement, the app or the payoff quote they followed.
themes.root_cause: Interest accrues daily until the payment posts and the grace period needs two full-payment cycles, but every balance the customer is shown is presented as if paying it ends the charge.
examples: Interest was charged two days after the bill was paid in full and on time, because the balance had to be paid in full for two consecutive months to stop interest.
Even after paying the full balance as instructed, the company kept charging $70.00 a month plus nearly $1700.00 in interest.

themes.name: Late fee for a payment the bank's own system failed to make
themes.problem_statement: Autopay, a scheduled payment or account access fails on the bank's side, and the late fee, returned-payment fee or interest that follows is left with the customer.
themes.root_cause: Payment automation and account blocks change or fail without alerting the customer, and the fee engine bills the missed payment without checking why it never went through.
examples: No reminder is sent on the day a payment is due, resulting in a $40.00 late fee the following day, which the customer believes is intentional.
The automatic payment for $7800.00 due was mistakenly only charged as $84.00, and the full $7800.00 was later withdrawn unexpectedly, driving the account negative.

themes.name: Paying twice to fix a travel booking the bank got wrong
themes.problem_statement: A trip or points transfer arranged through the bank's travel service fails, and the customer pays change fees, fare differences or the whole trip again to put it right.
themes.root_cause: Bookings and points transfers made through the travel portal are not reliably passed to the airline or partner, and nothing covers the costs the customer pays to repair them.
examples: A booking error meant the airline showed no payment on file at the gate, forcing a second $1,400.00 payment for flights already paid $1,300.00 through Chase.
Chase is requiring the customer to pay a fee to transfer liability before it will refund any of the credit for the flight it failed to ticket.

themes.name: Escrow billed for insurance the customer already has
themes.problem_statement: A lender-placed hazard or flood premium, and the escrow shortfall behind it, is added to the mortgage payment although the customer's own policy is on file.
themes.root_cause: Force-placed coverage is bought and billed through escrow on a lapse flag alone, without matching the policy or address evidence the customer has already sent.
examples: Chase purchased a flood insurance policy costing double the homeowner policy while covering less than the prior policy and its own appraisal value, weeks after ignoring the customer's emailed concerns.
Chase required expensive lender-placed insurance and would not release the Declaration page needed to get cheaper outside insurance.

themes.name: Quoted service price too high and not negotiable
themes.problem_statement: The price quoted for a service (setup, advisory, merchant, lockbox, expedited handling) is well above what the customer budgeted, and the agent can offer no discount.
themes.root_cause: Service pricing is set centrally with no discount authority on the front line and is only quoted once the customer asks, so the objection ends in a flat refusal.
examples: The $1,000 fee to establish the trust and the $200 to $500 a year to maintain it are higher than I expected, so I asked whether the fees could be reduced.
Transaction fees of 2-3%, assessment fees of $0.15 to $0.30 and chargeback fees of $20 to $50 are eating into his small business's profits, and he qualifies for no discounts.

themes.name: Upfront lending fee kept when the loan never closed
themes.problem_statement: A deposit or processing fee taken at the start of a loan application is kept even when the file never closes, and no one can explain what it paid for.
themes.root_cause: Application deposits are collected early, flagged non-refundable and disclosed late, and no process returns them when the bank or the deal fails to complete.
examples: A $500.00 charge for a simple pre-qualification letter needed during a divorce buyout was never properly explained despite multiple questions, and no help has been received.

A $650.00 nonrefundable lending deposit, never disclosed until a week into the process, was not refunded even after Chase ran into problems and the customer switched to another lender who closed on time.

themes.name: Paying a loan off early costs extra instead of less
themes.problem_statement: Clearing a loan ahead of schedule attracts a percentage penalty or carries fees and interest forward, so the customer saves nothing by paying early.
themes.root_cause: Loan contracts price prepayment penalties and front-loaded fees into the payoff quote with no interest rebate, and the front line cannot waive a contractual term.
examples: The $27,500 payoff with $2,500 of interest seems quite high, there is no discount for paying early, and $1,172.97 a month to finish in two years is more than I can afford.
My loan carries a prepayment penalty of 2% of the outstanding balance if I pay it off before maturity, and there is no way to avoid it.

themes.name: other: money_held_or_not_returned
themes.problem_statement: Statements about money held or not returned that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: a security review locked my account and my money with it
themes.problem_statement: The bank restricts, locks or closes the account after a security review and the customer cannot reach their money, often finding out only when a card or payment is declined.
themes.root_cause: Fraud and AML reviews restrict or close accounts before the customer is notified, and only a back office can lift the block, with no timeline and no interim access to the balance.
examples: My account has been on hold and I have not been able to access my funds for the past few days, and nobody told me why until I called.
The customer only learned his account had been suspended over unauthorized transactions from an email afterwards, with no notification before the suspension.

themes.name: my deposit is stuck pending or never posted at all
themes.problem_statement: Money that was paid in does not reach the balance: checks sit pending for days or weeks, or a deposit never posts at all, while the customer needs the funds.
themes.root_cause: Deposit holds run the full standard period and verification is manual, so funds stay unavailable even after the paying bank has cleared the item and no one can expedite the release.
examples: The customer's deposit had not been processed; the agent put it through on the call with the funds due to appear within the hour.
A $500 deposit made on Tuesday is still processing and will not be available for another 24 hours, but I need it verified now.

themes.name: a court order or tax levy froze my account with no warning
themes.problem_statement: A court garnishment or a tax levy freezes the account or takes the balance, and the customer often learns of it only when the money has already gone.
themes.root_cause: The bank must act on the order the day it arrives and cannot lift it without the creditor or the court, while the notice meant to warn the customer arrives late or never.
examples: The IRS placed a levy on my account over a $5,000 tax debt and I was told the funds cannot be released until the debt is paid in full.
The state has a garnishment on my account and the bank is holding my money under a court order, so I cannot use my own funds and their hands are tied.

themes.name: a payment that went out wrong and nobody can reverse
themes.problem_statement: A payment goes out wrong, to the wrong payee, or never reaches the merchant, and the customer cannot recover it; the dispute runs with no provisional credit.
themes.root_cause: Once a payment is processed the first point of contact has no reversal path, so recovery depends on the payee or on a dispute that gives the customer no money back meanwhile.
examples: After a leased vehicle's payoff was completed, Chase has not provided a payoff statement or final bill and appears to have sent the overpayment refund to the dealer instead of the customer.
The customer paid $1000 instead of $100 on a utility bill yesterday and the agent could not reverse it because the system does not allow reversals once processed.

themes.name: a fixed limit or rule stops me taking out my own money
themes.problem_statement: Withdrawal caps, expiry rules or the lack of a card stop the customer taking out money they already hold, and no exception can be made however urgent the need.
themes.root_cause: Fixed limits (Regulation D, daily caps, 90-day check expiry, card-only access) are enforced by the system with no exception route for a customer with an urgent, verified need.
examples: I need my own money now but I am told a federal rule limits what I can take out and that no exception can be made, after years as a loyal customer.
I asked for checks 1234, 5678 and 9012 to be reissued and was told they were stopped payments, so they cannot be reissued or refunded.

themes.name: the closing balance check they promised to mail never came
themes.problem_statement: The account is closed and the customer is told the remaining balance will be posted as a cashier's check within days or weeks; the check never comes and no one can trace it.
themes.root_cause: Closing balances are released by a back-office mailing process with no tracking, no ownership on the phone line and no trigger to chase an item that was never received.
examples: After closing the checking account, the customer was told a refund check for the remaining balance would be sent, but it never arrived.
The bank promised the remaining $3,600.00 balance would be mailed within three weeks, but after six weeks no check has arrived.

themes.name: my check stays held because the issuer cannot be reached
themes.problem_statement: A deposited check stays frozen for weeks because the fraud team cannot reach the issuer on the one number it holds, and every other proof the customer offers is refused.
themes.root_cause: Check verification accepts one channel only, an outbound call to a number the bank sourced itself, with no route for written or issuer-initiated proof when that number is wrong or dead.
examples: A deposited check's hold timeline kept getting pushed back, and Chase eventually said it could not verify the check with no written explanation or portion released.
Chase closed the checking account because a $75000.00 USDA treasury check could not be verified as legitimate, and has not released the check back to the customer.

themes.name: the ATM took my cash and never credited it
themes.problem_statement: Cash put into an ATM is not credited, or a failed withdrawal is debited anyway, and the temporary credit raised while it is investigated is taken back again.
themes.root_cause: ATM cash discrepancy claims are decided from the machine's own balancing record, so once it balances the customer's error receipt or the camera footage carries no weight.
examples: An ATM deposit of $9,500 in cash was credited only $8,500, and a $1,000 provisional credit issued for the shortage was later reversed.
An ATM deposit of $2,200.00 in cash intended for rent errored out, reset, and never issued a receipt, and the cash was never credited to the account.

themes.name: money already credited was taken back without warning
themes.problem_statement: A refund, dispute credit or deposit that had already landed in the balance is withdrawn again, usually with no notice, leaving the account short or overdrawn.
themes.root_cause: Provisional credits and accepted deposits are reversed automatically when a claim closes or the paying bank recalls the item, with no warning and no cover for the overdraft that follows.
examples: Another bank pulled back all her paychecks, which led Chase to close her checking account and left two credit cards maxed out, with Chase refusing to discuss the cause.
A fraud claim refund was fully processed into the account, then the same money was withdrawn back weeks later with no phone call, email, or text explanation.

themes.name: money sent to me reached the bank and then vanished
themes.problem_statement: Money confirmed to have left the sender reaches the bank but never shows in the account, and no one can say where it went or produce proof of what became of it.
themes.root_cause: Tracing an item across closed accounts, returned checks and older transactions needs records the front line cannot see, and no team owns finding money that fell between two systems.
examples: A $2,500.00 refund was issued by the merchant to an old, closed debit card, and Chase has no account history to trace it while the merchant provided proof of the refund.
Cashier's checks issued to the customer were never cashed and were returned to Chase, but the funds have still not been placed into any account years later.

themes.name: my closed account's balance held with no release date
themes.problem_statement: The account is closed and the balance left in it is kept under review or verification for weeks or months, with no reason given and no date when the money will be released.
themes.root_cause: Releasing the balance of a closed account sits with an internal department that nobody on the phone or in a branch can reach or chase, and no clock runs against the release.
examples: The customer needs the funds in the closed account to pay bills but was told they could not be released for no stated reason.
Over $300,000.00 across accounts that were closed and zeroed out has been withheld for months, with Chase saying only that they are trying to verify the customer.

themes.name: a deposit landed in an account already closed
themes.problem_statement: Pay, benefits or a deposit lands in an account the bank has already closed; it is neither handed to the customer nor sent back, and nobody can say where the money now sits.
themes.root_cause: Closing an account does not stop inbound credits being accepted, and no process returns a deposit that posts after closure, so it waits on a back office the customer cannot reach.
examples: Chase accepted a $500.00 direct deposit into the account about two weeks after it was claimed to be closed, and has not explained how or where the funds went.
The Chase account was closed less than 24 hours after opening, and Chase is refusing to send a check for the $330.00 unemployment deposit already in the account, sending it back to the state instead.

themes.name: my hold was extended past the date I was promised
themes.problem_statement: A deposit hold is pushed back or left open past the availability date the customer was given, with no written notice, no reason and no partial release of the funds.
themes.root_cause: Extended holds are set and prolonged by a back-office risk decision the branch and phone line cannot see or shorten, and the written notice and partial-release steps are never carried out.
examples: Even after all checks were manually verified as legitimate, Chase kept holding the funds for over 33 days, repeatedly pushing back the release date.
Checks deposited into the business account are held far longer than a normal transfer between banks should take, and the representative could not explain or justify it.

themes.name: I got back less than my balance with no breakdown
themes.problem_statement: The customer gets back less than the balance they held: money is applied to an alleged debt or simply missing, and no statement shows how the returned figure was worked out.
themes.root_cause: A back office nets the balance against a negative balance or an alleged loss before releasing it, and the closing payment goes out with no breakdown the customer can check or challenge.
examples: A fake loan scam led to bogus checks being deposited and money sent back out; Chase restricted the account, leaving it negative and refusing to return the customer's own $540.00.
The cashier's check eventually issued for the closed account came up short of the actual balance with no statement explaining the amount.

themes.name: closing the account wiped out the points I had earned
themes.problem_statement: The bank closes the account and the whole earned points balance disappears with it, with no warning and no chance to redeem or transfer the points first.
themes.root_cause: Closure voids the points balance the same day and the decision is never flagged in advance, so no redemption or transfer window is offered even to an account in good standing.
examples: She paid a $590 annual fee this year but could not use the card for the full year due to the closure, and wants it refunded along with her points.

After being encouraged by Chase to open a checking account for a promotion, the credit cards used to earn points for the same promotional push were closed for 'too many accounts,' forfeiting the earned points.

themes.name: points missing from my balance and redemptions frozen
themes.problem_statement: Points the customer earned or paid for are missing from the balance, and while the claim is looked at the rest of the points cannot be redeemed either.
themes.root_cause: Rewards balance corrections sit with a separate rewards investigation that locks redemptions and gives no timeline, so the customer misses the trip and pays another way.
examples: I am planning a trip and wanted to use my points to book flights, but no redemptions can be processed until the rewards balance is corrected.
Unable to resolve the points issue in time, the customer ended up paying out of pocket for flights for his wife and daughter to join the trip.

themes.name: my late relative's money that nobody will release
themes.problem_statement: After a death the family cannot get the money: a beneficiary designation blocks the transfer, or a payment confirmed as owed stays unpaid for months although every document was supplied.
themes.root_cause: Estate and beneficiary claims sit with a specialist back office that applies the designation with no waiver and works to no timetable, so the family gets neither a route nor a date.
examples: My mother has died and her accounts cannot be put in my name because they carry a beneficiary designation she never mentioned to me.
A pension payment of about $20,000.00 confirmed owed to her late mother has not been paid for over a year despite submitting every requested document, including death certificates.

themes.name: my matured bond or redemption payout stuck in processing
themes.problem_statement: Money owed on a matured bond, a redemption or an investment account is not paid out: the case sits in processing for weeks and any mismatch in the records adds another review.
themes.root_cause: Redemption and maturity payouts run on a fixed multi-week back-office cycle that nothing can expedite and that restarts whenever the holder's details do not match the register.
examples: After months of failed attempts to redeem his paper bonds, the customer was told the records show a different name and address, so a back-office review of several weeks is needed before anything can be paid.
The customer has waited weeks for a payment from the indemnity bond; the bond has been issued but is still in processing and nothing can be done to speed it up.

themes.name: other: no_response_or_follow_up
themes.problem_statement: Statements about no response or follow up that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: promised callback never comes and the customer chases
themes.problem_statement: An agent promises that someone will call back or that the matter is being handled, nothing happens, and the customer has to ring again and explain it from the start.
themes.root_cause: Callbacks are promised verbally without an owned, tracked task, so no queue picks the case up and nobody is accountable for closing the loop with the customer.
examples: A branch teller submitted an earlier payment incorrectly causing it to be declined, and complaints about it plus promised escalation callbacks were never returned.
The customer was told someone would get back to her about an issue that was supposed to be resolved last week, and no one ever reached out.

themes.name: what the agent promised on my last call was never done
themes.problem_statement: Something the customer asked for - a checkbook, alerts, a letter, information, a fix - is never done, and no confirmation ever tells them it failed.
themes.root_cause: Requests are captured as free-text notes on the account rather than as work items, so nothing drives them to completion and no failure notice is sent back.
examples: A Chase representative said he processed a refund of 3 late fees and return-payment fees, but it was never done and there is no record of it.
The PIN reminder that was supposedly sent on Friday never reached me by email or text, which is why I had to call back.

themes.name: a fee, flag or closure applied with no notice to me
themes.problem_statement: A fee, a fraud flag, a suspension or a charge-off happens with no notice first, and the customer finds out only by calling or from the damage already done.
themes.root_cause: The alerts and notice letters meant to precede these actions are not triggered or never delivered, and nothing checks that the customer was actually reached.
examples: Chase never sent any notice that a co-signed auto loan was past due, in collections, or charged off, and the customer only learned of it when their security clearance was put at risk.
Refund checks from cancelling extended warranty and tire protection were sent directly to the customer, and nobody told them the money had to go to Chase.

themes.name: the title or document I keep asking for never arrives
themes.problem_statement: Titles, lien releases, invoices, tax forms and claim evidence requested again and again never reach the customer, blocking whatever they need to do next.
themes.root_cause: Document requests are handed to a back office with no tracking or deadline, so the same request can be repeated for months or years without anything being produced.
examples: After a lease ended, a $1,900.00 tax and disposition fee bill was never sent as promised, though the customer requested an invoice before paying and offered to pay immediately upon receipt.
An auto loan paid off years ago still has no title provided by Chase, and a written request for leniency went unanswered.

themes.name: no one answers or calls back, every call ends in a transfer
themes.problem_statement: The customer spends days trying to reach someone; published and fraud-alert numbers go unanswered and every call ends in another transfer.
themes.root_cause: No one owns the case, so calls land in queues that are not answered and transfers pass the customer along instead of anyone taking the matter to a conclusion.
examples: I have been trying to get hold of someone all day and no one has returned my calls.
I have been trying to get hold of my bank for weeks and nobody returns my calls or emails, which is really frustrating.

themes.name: my case is still under investigation with no date given
themes.problem_statement: A claim, hold or review stays open for weeks or months; every call gets the same 'still investigating', with no date, no explanation and no way to tell whether anything is happening.
themes.root_cause: Case progress is not exposed to the people who answer the phone, and the original timeline is not tracked or re-committed when it slips, so agents can only tell the customer to wait.
examples: Multiple Chase agents told the customer she may not get her money back and offered no updates a week after promising a seven-to-ten day investigation.
After the misleading advice was acknowledged, only an apology was offered, and Chase's fraud review committee gave no timeline or guarantee of feedback.

themes.name: the team that decides my case takes no calls from anyone
themes.problem_statement: The department that actually decides takes no calls, emails or visitors, and neither the branch nor the phone agent can reach it, question its decision or say what it needs.
themes.root_cause: Back-office fraud, legal and review teams are deliberately kept off any inbound channel, with no internal case-handover route that lets the customer-facing staff put a question to them.
examples: Closing deceased parents' joint accounts and disbursing the funds has stalled for over two months after all documents were submitted, with the branch, back office and legal department passing the case around.
Despite submitting full legal guardianship documents for her mother twice, Chase keeps forwarding the case to its legal department with no resolution, jeopardizing court deadlines.

themes.name: the bank and the other party each point at the other
themes.problem_statement: The bank tells the customer to take it up with the merchant, the processor or the other bank, and that party sends them straight back, so nobody ever owns the problem.
themes.root_cause: No one is made responsible for a case that spans two institutions, so each side closes it as out of scope instead of contacting the other directly on the customer's behalf.
examples: Chase branches say the invoicing service is a separate company they cannot assist with, while the processor only accepts support tickets and has no phone number, leaving the customer with no clear path to resolution.
Another bank is holding the fraudulently deposited funds on the customer's behalf but cannot release them until Chase contacts them, which Chase refuses to do.

themes.name: my letters and written complaints are never answered
themes.problem_statement: Certified letters, emails and formal complaints to the executive or dispute office are never answered, so the customer has no written record and no way to escalate.
themes.root_cause: Written inbound channels have no intake queue, no response deadline and no owner, so correspondence is logged and closed without any reply ever being drafted.
examples: Money migrated to the new accounts was frozen for a while, and two written requests for the underlying policy have gone unanswered.
An Executive Office complaint was opened with a reference number, but no one has followed up.

themes.name: the paperwork I sent is lost and asked for all over again
themes.problem_statement: Faxed proof, filed claims and legal documents vanish: no record exists, the claim was never opened, and the customer is asked for the same paperwork over and over.
themes.root_cause: Documents arrive by fax, branch scan and phone claim into channels that do not attach them to a case record or acknowledge receipt, so nothing proves they were ever sent.
examples: A faxed transcript and paperwork from the merchant confirming the fraud and refund was never received by Chase across three attempts at two different branches.
Despite around 20 branch visits and submitting all legal paperwork, a deceased parent's funds have not been released, with the same unresolved lost-check form process repeated.

themes.name: told nothing can be done, and the call ends there
themes.problem_statement: The customer reports a scam, a still-pending transfer or a hardship and is told nothing can be done: no action is taken, no remedy offered, only advice to watch the account.
themes.root_cause: Front-line and dispute staff have no tool to stop a pending payment or reopen a closed claim, and no route to a team that does, so the call ends in advice instead of an action.
examples: After months of phone calls and documentation, Chase's only offer was to return the check, which is now stale and cannot fix the problem.
Immediately after the scam call, Chase said it could not help because the debit card was already closed, and only advised watching the account.

themes.name: the credit or bonus I was promised never reached my account
themes.problem_statement: A refund, courtesy credit or account bonus that an agent, supervisor or banker confirmed is still not on the account months later, and nobody can say why.
themes.root_cause: Promised credits and promotional bonuses are noted on the account but depend on a separate fulfilment step that nothing tracks, so the posting quietly fails with no notice to the customer.
examples: Neither the banker nor a phone specialist could fix the bonus issue, and the branch had no director to escalate to since the previous one had just resigned.
The branch manager said the remaining $1000.00 could not be retrieved for several more days and also failed to refund a $30.00 check order fee as promised.

themes.name: my card benefit claim is never decided, only re-documented
themes.problem_statement: A card benefit claim for a delayed trip, lost luggage or a rental runs for months: the same documents are asked for again or the claim is refiled under another cover, and nothing is decided.
themes.root_cause: Card benefit claims sit with an outsourced administrator whose only move is another document request, with no decision deadline and no route for the bank to settle the claim itself.
examples: Over several months, Chase repeatedly asked for additional information about the charges without ever specifying what was missing, despite the same documentation being resent multiple times.

A trip delay reimbursement claim was accidentally cancelled, could not be reopened, and had to be refiled multiple times under different claim types, with documents repeatedly reported as missing despite multiple resubmi

themes.name: my loan application passed its review date with no word
themes.problem_statement: A mortgage, HELOC or loan application passes the review time the customer was given with no word, and the phone line can only say it may still be in processing.
themes.root_cause: Application milestones are never pushed out to the customer and the processing status is not exposed to the front line, so nothing flags a file that has passed its own review date.
examples: I applied for a HELOC and had not heard anything at all, which was getting frustrating, so I had to call to ask what was happening.
I did not get the update I was expecting on my mortgage application, so I had to call to find out where it stands.

themes.name: no proof my disputed debt is owed, yet collection goes on
themes.problem_statement: A formal validation or identity-theft dispute produces no documentation showing the balance is owed, while the reporting and the collection activity carry on regardless.
themes.root_cause: Disputes are closed with a verification code instead of producing the underlying contract or statements, and nothing pauses reporting or collection while the request is outstanding.
examples: Despite a formal dispute and follow-up letter, JPMCB Card Service has not produced documentation verifying the disputed account as accurate.
A request for a 1099-C or written confirmation that a proven-fraudulent debt was cancelled and removed from credit reporting has gone unanswered.

themes.name: other: long_wait_or_delay
themes.problem_statement: Statements about long wait or delay that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: repeated identity questions before the request is started
themes.problem_statement: Before a simple request is even started the customer is asked for identifier after identifier, one at a time, and sometimes still cannot be verified at the end of it.
themes.root_cause: The verification script demands the full set of identifiers for every request whatever its risk, and agents work through them one by one instead of in a single step.
examples: I had to give my father's date of birth and social security number and then my own licence number and address before anything could move forward.
I just wanted direct deposit set up for my paycheck and instead had to give employer details, payroll contacts and confirm my own name and address.

themes.name: long hold ends in a transfer to another queue
themes.problem_statement: The customer waits on hold for twenty minutes to an hour and is then passed to another department, often to hold again, with the matter still unresolved.
themes.root_cause: Front-line agents are not authorised to complete most requests, so nearly every case is routed to a specialist queue and the customer pays for it in hold time.
examples: The customer had already been on the phone a while, answering verification questions and holding, before being transferred to technical support with the card still not working.
I waited on hold for over 30 minutes and then had to be transferred to the technical department instead of being helped.

themes.name: items only sent by post, days away, with no way to expedite
themes.problem_statement: Cards, checks, statements, titles, refunds and credits all take days or weeks to arrive by post or batch processing, and nothing can be expedited.
themes.root_cause: Fulfilment runs on fixed postal and batch cycles quoted as 3 to 10 business days, with no expedited channel offered even when the customer has run out of options.
examples: The customer felt the release process was slow, with a few days quoted and a further 3-5 business days to process the signed documents.
More than a year after paying off the car loan, Chase never sent the lien release letter or title, and even an overnight request takes two more days to process.

themes.name: investigation stays open with no date anyone can give
themes.problem_statement: An investigation, hold or suspension stays open and nobody can say when it will be decided or when the money or the access will come back.
themes.root_cause: Back-office teams work these cases without a published status or committed turnaround, so the agent on the phone has nothing to offer beyond saying that it varies.
examples: The check fraud claim I filed a few days ago is still under investigation and nobody can tell me when I will hear back, and I just want to know my money is safe.
With bills due today the customer was offered the mobile app or a branch visit, neither of which she can use, and no estimate of when online banking will be back.

themes.name: work promised on an earlier call is still not done
themes.problem_statement: A release, transfer, reactivation or setup promised a week or more ago still has not happened, and the customer only finds that out by calling again.
themes.root_cause: The follow-up task stalls between departments with no owner and no check that the quoted date was met, so nothing moves until the customer chases it themselves.
examples: After paying off my auto loan, the electronic lien release has been resubmitted by Chase multiple times, each promised within 7-10 business days, but the DMV still shows it as not released.
More than several weeks after Chase confirmed receiving the full auto loan payoff, the lien release and vehicle title still haven't been processed, and an escalation attempt went unanswered.

themes.name: money stays debited for weeks while the dispute is reviewed
themes.problem_statement: A disputed or unauthorised charge stays debited for weeks or months while the claim is investigated, with no provisional credit and no interim answer.
themes.root_cause: Provisional credit is not issued at claim intake unless a rule forces it, so the whole investigation window, often 30 to 90 days or more, runs at the customer's expense.
examples: A $60.00 charge for a purchase the customer never made is being handled only through a mailed paper form, with no reversal issued yet.
A $2,100.00 fraud claim was denied for months before Chase finally returned the money, and the customer never received the legally required written explanation for the initial denial.

themes.name: application stuck in review with no decision and no date
themes.problem_statement: An application or limit request stays 'in processing' past the few days quoted, with no decision, no date and no status the agent on the phone can see.
themes.root_cause: Decisioning queues have no customer-visible status and no committed turnaround, so agents can only repeat that volumes are high and that nothing can be expedited.
examples: Chase has unreasonably delayed opening a Qualified Income Trust account despite complete documentation and a valid Power of Attorney, causing about $5,200.00 in harm tied to Medicaid eligibility timing.
An ACH limit increase request for her trucking business, pending well beyond the stated two-to-three day timeline, has received no approval, denial, or written status update.

themes.name: closed-account balance returned only by check weeks later
themes.problem_statement: After the bank closes or restricts the account, the balance only comes back as a mailed check weeks later, after repeated internal verification the customer cannot influence.
themes.root_cause: Closed-account balances are released only by a back-office review followed by a postal check run, with no branch or electronic route and no committed date.
examples: After my business account was closed with no reason given, a promised ~$8,000.00 refund check has been stalled for over a month by a check-writer phone verification issue.
Chase said it would close the account and issue a check refund within business days, but the customer risks losing a business deal because of how long the funds are held up.

themes.name: deposit held for one to two weeks with no early release
themes.problem_statement: Deposited checks and ATM deposits are held for 8 to 14 days, or a promised temporary credit keeps being pushed back, so rent and bills cannot be paid.
themes.root_cause: Holds are set by amount and account history alone, with no way for an agent to verify a specific deposit and release it early once the funds are confirmed.
examples: Chase's 8-day holds on checks written on the account have prevented paying bills and rent, causing the loss of an apartment and significant stress.

An IRS check deposit has been held and unverified for three weeks, and the account was restricted then closed without notice, while Chase tries to verify it by email, a method the IRS doesn't support.

themes.name: payment posts days after the date the bank stated
themes.problem_statement: Transfers, payments, refunds and rewards post days after the date the app or the agent stated, causing late fees, bounced payments and missed benefits.
themes.root_cause: Posting depends on batch cycles and manual release steps that the quoted times do not reflect, and nothing flags a payment that misses its stated date.
examples: A $7,000.00 online transfer initiated Friday still had not posted by the promised Monday date, threatening a bounced tax payment to the IRS.
A mortgage payment sent through the Chase app took extra days to reach the mortgage bank, resulting in a $190.00 late fee, though the same payment method had never been late before.

themes.name: same documents requested again, restarting the review
themes.problem_statement: An assumption or application sits in underwriting for months while documents already sent are requested again, each round restarting the review.
themes.root_cause: Underwriting asks for documents piecemeal instead of issuing one complete list up front, and every new request resets the queue, so earlier documents go stale.
examples: The assumption process took nearly a year with repeated document requests, long inactivity, and being transferred between departments with no clear communication.
A court-ordered mortgage assumption has been stalled for over 135 days because Chase repeatedly requests the same documents and lacks staff to process assumptions.

themes.name: earliest available appointment is days or weeks away
themes.problem_statement: The only route is an appointment or a place in a queue, and the earliest slot is days or weeks out while the customer needs it the same day.
themes.root_cause: Branch, advisor and specialist capacity is booked solid, with no same-day overflow, no phone alternative and no priority route for urgent cases.
examples: My car is totalled but it may take a few days just to schedule an adjuster, and I am being asked for photos and repair estimates on top.
The earliest advisor appointment is two weeks away and nobody will give me even basic information over the phone, which I cannot wait for.

themes.name: estate and authority changes wait weeks on signed paperwork
themes.problem_statement: Estate, power of attorney and authority changes are blocked behind notarised forms, in-person signatures or a legal review that takes weeks.
themes.root_cause: These requests are gated by wet-signature, notarised or court paperwork and a legal review queue, with no digital route and no expedited handling.
examples: After weeks of waiting it will still take a few more days once the fax arrives, and it cannot be expedited because of the legal review.
I need the letter urgently but it cannot be issued without the forms, so I have to wait 3-5 business days after returning them.

themes.name: call drops during hold or transfer and must be restarted
themes.problem_statement: The call is cut off while the customer holds or is transferred, or the published number simply goes unanswered, so the whole call has to start again.
themes.root_cause: Transfers and overflow calls are dropped rather than queued, and no callback or warm handover is offered, so the customer has no way back into the case.
examples: The transfer to the Payroll Department disconnected, so the customer was left holding and had to be transferred a second time before she hung up.
I was on hold for a while about corporate banking services and the call suddenly got disconnected, so I had to call back.

themes.name: full eligibility questionnaire before the request is started
themes.problem_statement: A customer with an urgent need must first answer a full run of eligibility, employment, income and purpose questions and supply proof before the request is even started.
themes.root_cause: Intake scripts collect the complete qualification set up front for every request, with no short path for small or urgent cases and no way to start the case while details are gathered.
examples: I asked to be put straight through to someone who handles wealth management and was held up by questions about what I was looking for.
The customer was given three scholarship options but wanted to be told outright which one she qualifies for, and was impatient at the eligibility questions and the weeks-long application process.

themes.name: other: incorrect_or_conflicting_information
themes.problem_statement: Statements about incorrect or conflicting information that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: a different answer from every agent I speak to
themes.problem_statement: Each call, transfer or branch visit produces a different answer about the same request, so the customer never learns which answer is the true one.
themes.root_cause: There are no shared case notes or single authoritative source across agents and channels, so every contact improvises its own answer from scratch.
examples: Despite the vehicle being paid off in full, Chase has given repeated conflicting and incorrect instructions about submitting lien release documentation to the state DMV, and still hasn't submitted it.
Chase claims debt collectors have not called about this matter, though he has received multiple collection calls over the last two years.

themes.name: the rate or fee I was promised at signing never applied
themes.problem_statement: What the customer was told when opening or signing - rate, fee, promotion, first payment date - differs from the terms the account actually applies.
themes.root_cause: Sales and mailer wording is never checked against the booked product terms, so verbal or printed promises are not reflected in the system.
examples: A 'Just For You' pre-screening offer implied pre-approval for an auto loan, but the application was denied after applying.
The dealer said the auto loan had 90 days with no payment due, but Chase Auto began billing after only 45 days and charged late fees.

themes.name: wrong details on my file misinform me and block me
themes.problem_statement: Balances, dates, addresses, routing numbers, accounts or security details on file contradict what the customer knows, blocking verification or misinforming them.
themes.root_cause: Customer and account data is captured or migrated incorrectly and never reconciled, so the system of record drifts from reality with no route to correct it.
examples: I have had an auto loan since 2015 and a personal loan since 2017 with this bank, but the system shows no active loans under my name at all.

Attempts to resolve an issue involving the registered phone number of a car's purchaser were rejected by the fraud department as invalid, and the account remains restricted after the car had to be reported stolen.

themes.name: told it was resolved, then billed or reported anyway
themes.problem_statement: After the bank confirms a charge is dropped, a loan closed or a payment arrangement agreed, the amount comes back with fees or a late mark on the credit file.
themes.root_cause: Resolutions agreed by phone are not written into billing and collections, so the original balance keeps running and reporting unchanged.
examples: Chase accepted nearly $5000.00 in payments on an auto loan that had secretly been charged off 10 months earlier, then attempted repossession and demanded $27000.00 to reinstate the loan.
The customer's credit score kept dropping from late payments on a totaled vehicle's loan that they and their mother believed GAP insurance had paid off.

themes.name: I had to call again because the last call answered nothing
themes.problem_statement: The customer has to call back because the previous contact gave no clear or complete answer to the same question.
themes.root_cause: Agents lack the knowledge or system access to answer these questions at first contact, and nothing is logged for anyone to follow up.
examples: Customer previously called the bank about concerns for her mother's accounts, but no one seemed to know what she was talking about.

Every login to online banking said the username and password were incorrect and several password resets changed nothing, because business accounts need a different login than the personal one he was using.

themes.name: my claim denied for a reason that contradicts my evidence
themes.problem_statement: A fraud or dispute claim is denied, or its credit reversed, on a reason that contradicts the evidence, and no record of the investigation is ever shown to the customer.
themes.root_cause: Claim decisions are taken from merchant replies or automated rules without reading the customer's evidence, and the denial reason is never checked against the case file.
examples: Chase closed the account and falsely claimed to have credited a $220.00 dispute that was never actually reflected on the account.

An $800.00 unauthorized Apple Pay charge's temporary credit was reversed because the customer had made other authorized transfers to their daughter, not because this specific charge was found authorized.

themes.name: the proof you demand changes at every contact
themes.problem_statement: To release funds or lift a restriction the bank demands verification that changes at each contact, or that an issuer or agency cannot give, so nothing the customer provides is enough.
themes.root_cause: Verification of held funds has no fixed checklist of accepted evidence, so each reviewer adds a new requirement and nobody can declare the customer verified.
examples: Chase claims to have called the landlord and employer to verify checks, but both say they were never asked the needed questions, or in one case never called at all, and Chase won't disclose the numbers it uses.
The bank had already verified the grandfather's identity and confirmed his retirement payments were not fraud in person, but later treated the same relationship as unverified again.

themes.name: told my deposit had cleared, then it was taken back
themes.problem_statement: A deposit shown as available and confirmed as cleared is reversed days later, after the customer has spent or wired it on that confirmation, and the loss stays with them.
themes.root_cause: Displayed availability and agent confirmations are read as settlement although the item can still be returned, and nobody checks the deposit has settled before calling it good.
examples: Multiple Chase employees repeatedly and explicitly assured that a check from India could 'definitely' be processed and funded within weeks, inducing the customer to open an account and spend thousands of dollars from a l
A $4,500.00 job-related check's hold was removed after being told the funds had been collected, but the check bounced weeks later, leaving the customer liable for money already wired out.

themes.name: condition disclosed only after it blocked the request
themes.problem_statement: A condition that decides the outcome, such as a hold after a card renumber or in-branch-only closure above a limit, is only revealed once it has already blocked the customer.
themes.root_cause: Conditions attached to a product or an action are not stated when the request is taken, only quoted afterwards to explain why the outcome differs from what was expected.
examples: The customer called to set up a joint checking account but learned an in-person visit to a branch is required, contrary to her expectation of completing it over the phone.
After the same representative helped renumber the account, every transaction was declined because of an undisclosed 24-48 hour hold, on top of previous false promises from the same person.

themes.name: told the request was done when it was never submitted
themes.problem_statement: The customer is told the check was mailed, the claim filed or the documents received, and only learns weeks later, after chasing it, that none of it ever happened.
themes.root_cause: Agents read a queued task as a completed one, and nothing confirms the check run, the claim submission or the document receipt before the customer is told it is done.
examples: A claim for $2000.00 in unauthorized transactions was reported as denied within a day with no notice, and a second representative later discovered the original claim had never actually been submitted.
The claim was only given a verbal reference number, with no written confirmation and no way to track the status until a decision is mailed.

themes.name: missing money blamed on the merchant or the other bank
themes.problem_statement: The bank blames the merchant, the other bank or a government agency for the missing money or the block, and that party says it never happened.
themes.root_cause: Agents explain a hold or a missing payment by pointing at the counterparty without tracing it with them, so nobody owns the trace across the two institutions.
examples: Chase claimed a merchant stole his refund, involving him in a dispute call, when Chase already had the money and was mailing a cashier's check that arrived days later.
Chase cancelled a verified external transfer after a fraud dept rep falsely claimed the other bank would not allow it, and never attempted the withdrawal.

themes.name: no written proof of payment a third party will accept
themes.problem_statement: The customer needs written evidence of a payment, a mailing or a decision to show a third party, and the bank offers only a partial image or a verbal account.
themes.root_cause: Confirmations exist only as agent notes and internal images; there is no customer-facing letter, tracking number or reference the customer can hand to anyone else.
examples: A $30.00 check written to a state health department was debited from the account, but the provided check image lacks the payee account number, deposit date and payer information needed to confirm it reached the agency.
The bank could not provide any tracking number for the replacement check forms, leaving the customer unable to confirm whether the documents were ever sent.

themes.name: one team's approval reversed by another team days later
themes.problem_statement: An account or arrangement one team opened, approved or assured in writing is closed, refused or reversed days later by another team, with no new facts and no explanation.
themes.root_cause: Onboarding, fraud and branch teams decide independently and none is bound by, or even sees, the approval or assurance another has already given the customer.
examples: A phone representative twice assured the account would not close while an insurance refund was being investigated, but the account was closed anyway.
Chase closed the account for the exact activity, accepting payments for business sales, that a branch associate had specifically assured the customer was permitted.

themes.name: quoted policy contradicts the published terms
themes.problem_statement: A refusal or limit is justified by a policy, time limit or legal rule that contradicts the published terms, the regulation, or what the bank itself does in comparable cases.
themes.root_cause: Staff quote internal rules of thumb from memory without checking them against the published terms or the governing regulation, and nothing forces the quoted rule to match the case.
examples: Despite providing death certificates and letters of administration proving the joint account passed entirely to the father under survivorship, Chase is incorrectly applying a 120-hour simultaneous death rule and will rel

Chase treated a daughter's college account, which is not the customer's money, as the source of the required $2100.00 legal exemption, while treating the full business account balance as available for the levy.

themes.name: bonus never posts after the offer terms were met
themes.problem_statement: The customer meets the advertised spend or referral terms, but the bonus, points or cash back never posts, and each contact gives a different reason why it does not count.
themes.root_cause: Offer qualification is scored by a tracking rule (eligible spend, dates, purchase count) that nobody reconciles with the offer wording the customer was shown before refusing the bonus.
examples: I have had no rewards points on my credit card purchases for three months, and I am told it is because I missed a minimum spend I am sure I met.

Five identical $300.00 purchases made the same day to trigger a 10% cash back offer were paid on three cards but denied on two, with Chase giving inconsistent explanations about the offer's expiration.

themes.name: interest still charged after paying exactly as instructed
themes.problem_statement: Payments and credits land on a different balance than the customer intended, or the grace period is lost, so interest and plan fees keep accruing although they paid exactly as instructed.
themes.root_cause: Promotional, instalment and revolving balances follow an internal payment-allocation and grace-period hierarchy that is neither disclosed nor reflected in what agents tell customers to pay.
examples: Despite following a representative's advice on how to avoid interest during a $15000.00 balance transfer promotion, the customer was charged interest for several months.
A credit for a canceled purchase was applied to an interest-free extended payment plan instead of the original purchase, due to buried terms stating credits apply to the loan first.

themes.name: points shown as available are refused at redemption
themes.problem_statement: The rewards balance the customer is shown cannot actually be used: redemption is refused for insufficient points, or the advertised transfer stalls or is capped by limits nobody mentioned.
themes.root_cause: The points balance on display and the redemption engine apply different counts, exclusions and timings, and neither is reconciled before the customer is told what they can redeem.
examples: The offers in the mail say I can earn points towards cash back, but when I tried to redeem them it was a total hassle because of restrictions and limits.
My rewards balance online said I had enough points for a $25 gift card, but when I tried to redeem it I was told I did not have enough points.

themes.name: nobody can explain how the billed amount was calculated
themes.problem_statement: Statement, plan or interest figures contradict each other or the customer's own arithmetic, and neither phone nor branch staff can see or explain how the amount was produced.
themes.root_cause: Instalment plan and interest calculations run in a billing engine no frontline tool exposes, so agents can only restate the total and nobody owns reconciling it with the statement.
examples: Customer needs an explanation for 'variable principal balance' and why their credit card interest rate increased, but cannot get specific details over the phone without providing SSN.
The phone representative gave three different and incorrect answers about what balance the interest was calculated on, none matching the amount shown on the statement.

themes.name: the action taken does not match the instruction given
themes.problem_statement: A clear instruction - decline the offer, close the account, cut only this one limit - is carried out as something else, and the customer only finds out from the result.
themes.root_cause: Requests are re-keyed into the servicing system without reading the exact scope back to the customer, and nothing checks the action taken against the instruction given.
examples: Despite knowing about the divorce and the prior request to close the account, Chase tried to convince the ex-husband to keep the new account open.

Despite explicit instructions only to link accounts for point transfers, an agent added the customer as an authorized user, then falsely claimed the customer requested it before denying doing it at all.

themes.name: contact and data-sharing opt-outs acknowledged then ignored
themes.problem_statement: A formal request about how the bank contacts the customer or shares their data - written-only contact, cease communication, an opt-out - is acknowledged and then ignored.
themes.root_cause: Standing requests arrive as correspondence and are never turned into a flag on the account, so calls, letters and data sharing carry on exactly as before.
examples: Despite explaining an inability to complete standard phone verification and requesting written or secure communication only, the customer continues to be directed to phone support.
The institution failed to honor a formal opt-out instruction against sharing or reporting the customer's nonpublic personal information.

themes.name: letter asserts a payment or notice that never happened
themes.problem_statement: A letter, notice or formal response asserts a payment, a notice sent, a contact made or a document signed that the bank's own file, or the named third party, says never happened.
themes.root_cause: Letters, complaint responses and servicing documents are produced from templates and assumed-completed tasks, with nobody checking the assertions against the account file first.
examples: Chase, named as the depository for the mortgage trust, issued two formal denials that no account, note, or mortgage data exists in its systems for the property.

Chase never notified the customer of an 11-month lapse in mortgage insurance despite an email warning it about the coverage problem, then took $2,100.00 from escrow to buy a policy backdated to cover that period, which n

themes.name: other: denied_or_declined_without_explanation
themes.problem_statement: Statements about denied or declined without explanation that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: identity check fails and no other proof is accepted
themes.problem_statement: Every detail the customer gives fails the identity check, so the request is refused outright and no other way to prove who they are is offered.
themes.root_cause: Verification depends on data on file that is stale, wrong or never held, and agents have no fallback route, so any mismatch ends the call.
examples: The customer called to set up graduated savings rates and nothing could be done because the agent's system would not let her account be opened without verification.
A customer of over 10 years cannot be verified on her only account number, address or date of birth, so the agent will not renew her certificate of deposit.

themes.name: a fee waiver refused on policy alone, whatever my record
themes.problem_statement: A fee waiver, better rate or one-off exception is refused on policy grounds alone, and years as a customer or a clean record count for nothing in the answer.
themes.root_cause: Front-line agents have no discretion and no approval route for exceptions, so the policy is quoted instead of a decision being taken.
examples: I asked for emergency cash and was told the bank has strict policies on disbursing large amounts, even though I have banked here for years and gave all my details.
I need a letter showing my credit history and outstanding debts for a business loan, but you will only confirm that the account exists and its current balance.

themes.name: payments still demanded on a car a recall made unusable
themes.problem_statement: Deferment or hardship help is refused although the vehicle is unusable through a recall or a known defect, or the customer has documented a temporary loss of income.
themes.root_cause: Hardship criteria ignore vehicle inoperability and are applied without reviewing the evidence the customer submits, and no partial or reduced payment option is offered.
examples: A car is non-functional due to a known manufacturer software issue with no service being offered, and Chase, the loan holder, has been asked to hold the loan payment but has not accommodated this.

Despite an active year-long recall and repeated safety defects making the leased vehicle unsafe and unable to generate income, Chase Auto has not delayed the payment schedule to reflect its inoperability.

themes.name: card or online access blocked for a reason nobody explains
themes.problem_statement: The account, card or online access is frozen, declined or refused for security reasons that are never explained, leaving the customer locked out with nothing to correct.
themes.root_cause: Fraud and security rules raise blocks whose reason is not exposed to front-line agents, so no one on the call can explain the block or lift it.
examples: My online purchase was declined, I was told there were no issues with my account, and the next day I got an email saying the account had been frozen for suspicious activity.
Customer's account services were suspended by the system for security reasons, preventing access online and via the mobile app, but the agent resolved the issue.

themes.name: cannot be done by phone, go to a branch or write in
themes.problem_statement: A routine request cannot be carried out on the channel the customer is using, and the only answer is a branch visit, another number or a written request they may not be able to make.
themes.root_cause: Phone agents lack the entitlements to carry out these tasks, and no alternative is arranged for customers who cannot use the other channel.
examples: The customer was told calls cannot be transferred between departments and that he must call the CD service line himself to renew his CD.
The agent would not process a stop payment on a check I issued last week and could not even put a note on my account, telling me to visit a branch or mail a written request.

themes.name: claim denied on your records, my evidence never looked at
themes.problem_statement: A fraud or dispute claim is refused on the bank's own card, device or merchant records, while the documents, logs, footage and witnesses the customer offers are never examined.
themes.root_cause: Claim outcomes are decided from transaction and merchant data alone, and the process has no step for taking in the customer's evidence or answering it in the decision.
examples: The bank cannot stop fraudulent checks from clearing without a police report and signed fraud affidavit, which the customer finds cumbersome.
The bank requires initiating a dispute process and cannot immediately refund unauthorized pre-authorized debits without proof of fraudulent transactions.

themes.name: every account closed for good, no reason and no appeal
themes.problem_statement: The bank ends the relationship, sometimes every account at once or days after opening, gives no reason at any level of escalation, and offers no appeal or way back.
themes.root_cause: Exit decisions are taken by a risk team whose reasons the terms allow the bank to withhold, so no agent, banker or executive can review them or discuss them.
examples: A 15-year account was automatically closed after months of fraudulent transactions traced to a data leak, with remaining funds to be mailed by check.
The customer received a notice that the accounts would close within 10 business days with no reason provided, threatening the ability to pay past-due rent.

themes.name: deposit held until a third party's phone number verifies
themes.problem_statement: A deposited check is held and the account restricted until a third party's phone number verifies in the bank's system; it never does, and ID, phone bills or the person themselves are refused.
themes.root_cause: Check verification depends on matching a postpaid phone number to the endorser in an external database, and no alternative evidence is accepted when that match fails.
examples: A life insurance claim check endorsed via power of attorney led to restricted accounts, and despite notarized POA, the beneficiary's registered phone number, and an offer for the beneficiary to personally verify, Chase s
Despite providing IDs, pay stubs, and proof of joint account ownership, the funds remained blocked because the co-depositor's phone number could not be verified.

themes.name: refused on unnamed criteria, with no way to challenge it
themes.problem_statement: An application, programme or bonus is refused with only a generic message or a bare mention of criteria, and nobody will say which criterion failed or how to put it right.
themes.root_cause: Decisioning rules and adverse reasons are not exposed to the staff facing the customer, so the refusal is delivered without its specific ground or any route to challenge it.
examples: Customer called to inquire about community programs advertised via email, but was informed they do not meet the criteria for any current programs.

Three banks denied opening a checking account citing delinquency, despite having a full-time job and only small, unrelated collection accounts totaling less than the equivalent of a redacted small amount.

themes.name: a large deposit clears, then the account is frozen anyway
themes.problem_statement: A large check or wire is confirmed good and even cleared, then the account is restricted or the card cancelled anyway, locking the customer out of money the bank already accepted.
themes.root_cause: Risk rules fire on deposit size and re-open items that have already cleared, with no way to pre-clear an expected large deposit or to close the review once it is verified.
