examples: A $30000.00 legal settlement check deposited in person with both mother and son presenting ID and signing was still flagged for a fraud alert and the account restricted, despite an initial promise it would clear.

After Chase confirmed a $77000.00 home-sale check was good and raised the spending limit, the account was restricted and the debit card cancelled, even after supervisors verified the check with the title company.

themes.name: the footage or record that proves my case is withheld
themes.problem_statement: The footage, the cashing details, the recorded call or the letter that would prove the customer's case is held by the bank, and it will not release any of it to them.
themes.root_cause: Records that could settle a dispute are treated as internal and released only to a court or the police, with no process for giving the customer their own evidence.
examples: The bank would not provide details like where the check was cashed, information the customer needed to obtain camera footage and fight the case.
The bank told the customer that reviewing the ATM and drive-thru cameras that could confirm the deposit would require a lawyer and a court order.

themes.name: I reported the fraud and my accounts were closed days later
themes.problem_statement: Days after the customer reports fraud, disputes a charge or asks for help, every account is frozen or closed, as if raising the problem were the problem.
themes.root_cause: Claim and complaint activity feeds the same risk model that decides exits, so a customer who reports losses is scored as a risk and quietly offboarded.
examples: After reporting fraudulent checks posted to a son's account, the bank closed two accounts holding money for a mother's emergency care and her social security funds.
After reporting the scam, Chase closed both the original and a newly opened account and is refusing to let the customer open any account with them again, while still holding a cashier's check.

themes.name: one missed verification call and the claim is closed
themes.problem_statement: The claim is closed and the temporary credit reversed because the customer did not answer one verification call, with no voicemail, no email and no second attempt.
themes.root_cause: Claim verification is attempted only by outbound phone in office hours, and a non-answer is recorded as failure to cooperate, which closes the case automatically.
examples: A $90.00 charge made without consent was temporarily credited, then reversed back to the merchant because the customer did not respond to a phone call in time, and the merchant keeps billing monthly.
Chase closed the fraud claim after calling twice during working hours for a scan number that went unanswered, then charged the transaction again.

themes.name: certified documents refused because your system disagrees
themes.problem_statement: Government filings, certified documents and proof of ownership are handed over and refused because the bank's own system or data supplier shows something different, so nothing is accepted.
themes.root_cause: Verification checks compare only against internal or contracted data sources, and staff have no route to accept an authoritative document that contradicts what those sources return.
examples: Even after updating the LLC's official government filing to include the owner's phone number, Chase still would not accept it because its own system couldn't find it.

A $2000.00 transfer to the customer's own external account was rejected because Chase said the account name didn't match, and it was rejected again for the same reason even after proving ownership in branch.

themes.name: dispute refused as out of time, so nobody looks at it
themes.problem_statement: A fraud or billing dispute is refused as out of time, on a window counted from a date the bank chose, and that refusal takes the place of any look at the charges themselves.
themes.root_cause: Claim intake applies an age rule before any review, and nobody checks which date the clock ran from or whether the regulation still allows the report.
examples: Chase refused to investigate the unauthorized recurring charges as outside its 2-year dispute window, despite clear written proof the charges were unauthorized and concealed.
A $510.00 unauthorized transaction made after the debit card was stolen has not been investigated because Chase says the claim window hasn't passed, even though only 18 days have gone by.

themes.name: no claim is even opened, go settle it with the merchant
themes.problem_statement: The bank refuses to log or investigate the reported error at all and sends the customer to settle it with the merchant themselves, so no claim, credit or decision ever exists.
themes.root_cause: Claim intake filters out whole categories, such as small ACH debits, merchant service disputes and scams, before a case is created, and agents cannot escalate what it rejects.
examples: Chase's claims department refused to open a claim for a $33.00 ACH charge where the merchant failed to provide the paid-for service, despite Regulation E requiring the bank to log and investigate reported errors.
An internet bill payment was misapplied to a wireless account instead, forcing a double payment, but Chase closed the dispute claim and told the customer to resolve it directly with the merchant.

themes.name: staff demand a condition the published rules never set
themes.problem_statement: Staff refuse to open the account or complete the request unless the customer meets a condition the bank's own published rules and website do not require, and no rule is ever shown.
themes.root_cause: There is no published checklist staff must work to when opening accounts or taking requests, so individual employees add conditions of their own that nobody can source.
examples: Chase issued its own $8200.00 cashier's check but then refused to honor it when presented, insisting the customer reopen a business account that had been lawfully closed months earlier.
A teller repeatedly said a green card was required to open a business account despite the customer being a US citizen, never checked identification, and discouraged the application.

themes.name: the cover that came with the card pays little or nothing
themes.problem_statement: A travel insurance, purchase protection or trip benefit claim is refused, or settled far below the documented loss, on exclusions and limits the customer was never shown.
themes.root_cause: Benefit claims are decided by a separate insurer or administrator against terms never surfaced at sale, and nobody the customer can reach can explain the exclusion or the shortfall.
examples: A Chase Travel agent said any trip cancellation would be fully covered by the card, but after cancelling due to a passport problem, Chase denied the $2900.00 claim, saying passport-related cancellations are not covered.
Despite paying a $95.00 annual fee specifically for 2 United Club passes, the customer was denied lounge access as full while others were admitted, and Chase refused to extend the expiring passes.

themes.name: I met the offer's terms and the bonus never posted
themes.problem_statement: A bonus, cashback offer or statement credit the customer met the advertised terms for never posts, and the refusal turns on an activation or coding detail they could not see.
themes.root_cause: Reward eligibility is read from an offer-activation record agents cannot see or correct, so a purchase that met the advertised terms is scored as non-qualifying.
examples: Baggage fees totaling $120.00 were charged across three flights despite paying with the credit card that promises a free checked bag, and hours of calls between Chase and the airline resolved nothing.

A 10% cashback offer on a $340.00 hotel booking made through the provided activation link was denied after an investigation, and no one, including the Executive Office, could say what requirement was supposedly not met.

themes.name: the benefit claim dies on an exclusion nobody mentioned
themes.problem_statement: A travel, purchase protection or rental claim under the card's own benefits is denied on an exclusion, a reclassification or a missing form, and the documents sent with it go unanswered.
themes.root_cause: Benefit claims are adjudicated by a separate administrator against an exclusion checklist, with no step for weighing the customer's evidence and no real appeal.
examples: A $4,000.00 travel insurance claim was paid at only $1,000.00 because it was ruled a trip delay rather than a cancellation, despite an official document confirming the flight was cancelled.
The card's insurance partner is denying a rental damage claim on a technicality despite a signed rental agreement proving the card secured the rental and was charged for the damage.

themes.name: hardship plan refused though my loss of income is proven
themes.problem_statement: A hardship plan, lower settlement or payment arrangement is refused, or revoked without notice, although the loss of income is documented and the customer offers what they can pay.
themes.root_cause: Hardship and settlement eligibility follows undisclosed internal criteria that collections staff can neither explain nor override, so documented hardship never reaches a decision.
examples: Despite documenting complete unemployment with no income, Chase refused a lower lump-sum settlement offer and only proposed a $2,400.00 lump sum or a payment plan, both unaffordable.

Despite proactively contacting Chase before missing a payment and four separate follow-up attempts over a year, no hardship assistance was ever offered, and fees and interest now make up nearly half of the balance.

themes.name: we do not do that, and nowhere else is suggested
themes.problem_statement: The customer asks for something the bank simply does not provide - damaged notes, emergency cash, budgeting help, a language, trust advice - and is left with no alternative at all.
themes.root_cause: Out-of-scope requests have no owning service and agents hold no vetted list of internal or external alternatives, so a flat refusal ends the call.
examples: I needed $500 of worn-out currency replaced and after two departments I still have the same worn-out notes and no way to exchange them.
I have a $20 bill torn in half and was told the bank cannot exchange it and that I have to take it to the Federal Reserve myself.

themes.name: locked out of a trust account I am named on
themes.problem_statement: The grantor or named beneficiary of a trust account is refused every time they try to withdraw or change a beneficiary, and gets only a permissions error with no explanation.
themes.root_cause: Fiduciary account roles are set up so the customer's entitlements do not match their legal standing, and no team owns correcting the permission or explaining it.
examples: Every attempt to take money from the special-needs trust account returns an insufficient permissions error even though the customer is the primary beneficiary.
I keep getting denied access when I try to change the beneficiary on my trust account, even though I am the grantor on the account.

themes.name: no idea what I can borrow until the full file is in
themes.problem_statement: The customer asks what they could borrow and gets no indicative figure, and no route past the pre-qualified cap, until full documentation and a credit pull are in.
themes.root_cause: Pre-qualification tools return a figure only from a complete file, and agents are not allowed to give a ballpark range from what the customer has already told them.
examples: The agent would not give even a rough idea of the pre-approval amount without the full documentation in front of him.
You have pre-qualified me for up to $350,000 at 3.75% and that is not enough; I want to borrow more than that.

themes.name: my wire is somewhere in the bank and nobody will trace it
themes.problem_statement: A wire or commercial payment is blocked, missing or unreturned, and the bank gives no trace, no written status and no reason, even when the sending bank says it holds the money.
themes.root_cause: Wire investigations sit with a back office that has no customer-facing output, so front-line staff cannot see where the payment is and recall requests are refused unexplained.
examples: A commercial payment for civilian equipment has been blocked for an extended period, and while the sending bank confirms the funds are held at JPMorgan Chase, Chase says it does not see or hold them.
A $38000.00 wire transfer sent to Chase was never received by the intended recipient, and Chase rejected the recall request without explanation.

themes.name: no supervisor will come to the phone
themes.problem_statement: The customer asks to be escalated and is told no supervisor is available, or that the front line must review and approve the issue first, so the call ends where it started.
themes.root_cause: Escalation is rationed by the front line and supervisors take no direct calls, so there is no guaranteed route to a decision-maker when an agent cannot help.
examples: Customer was unable to speak to a supervisor because supervisors are also affected by the technical difficulties and not available.
Customer was denied speaking with a supervisor, as issues must be reviewed and approved by customer service first.

themes.name: other: system_or_app_failure
themes.problem_statement: Statements about system or app failure that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Login rejected as a wrong password and resets do not help
themes.problem_statement: Every login is rejected as an incorrect username or password although the details are right, and password resets do not restore access.
themes.root_cause: A block or bad flag on the online banking profile makes authentication fail whatever the credentials, and self-service resets do not clear it.
examples: I have been trying to set up a new account online but the website keeps rejecting my login and password, and resetting it several times did not help.
I got an email saying my card had expired and I needed to update my information, but when I tried to log in it said my password was incorrect.

themes.name: ATM fails mid-transaction and keeps my cash or card
themes.problem_statement: The ATM fails mid-transaction: no cash is dispensed, the deposit is refused or the card is rejected or captured, and nobody can retrieve them.
themes.root_cause: Faulty or offline machines are not taken out of service, and branch and phone agents have no route to release the cash or the card.
examples: I tried to deposit a check but the ATM kept saying error and would not take my card, and a branch visit and the customer service line did not work either.
I tried to withdraw cash at the Main and Elm ATM about 30 minutes ago and it did not dispense the money, and nobody can get it out for me.

themes.name: Online and app features fail with a bare error every time
themes.problem_statement: An online or app feature - adding a payee, a transfer, a mobile deposit, an alert, an application - fails on every attempt with a bare error and no reason.
themes.root_cause: Back-end failures surface as a generic error with no diagnosis, and the known defects sit unfixed with no date, so the customer has to call.
examples: Customer is unable to redeem points from their rewards checking account for weeks, receiving an 'invalid request' error and being kicked back to the login page.
I have tried to set up bill pay several times on the online banking platform and every time it shows an error and freezes.

themes.name: Statement and transaction downloads arrive corrupt
themes.problem_statement: Statement and transaction exports fail or open as corrupt files in every browser and on every computer, so the customer cannot reconcile their accounts.
themes.root_cause: The export and OFX service is broken or out of step with the file formats the customer's software expects, and no fix date is given.
examples: Every statement download comes through as file corrupt in Quicken, on different days and different computers, and I am running the latest version.
Transactions were not downloading properly due to a system issue, causing the customer frustration and requiring manual intervention.

themes.name: Debited for a payment that failed, or charged twice
themes.problem_statement: A payment is taken or taken twice while the transaction itself fails, or a credit that was due is never applied, leaving the customer out of pocket.
themes.root_cause: Payment processing errors are never reconciled against what was actually debited, so the failed leg is not reversed and the credit is not posted.
examples: I set up a direct debit and had a confirmation email, but it does not show on my account for last Wednesday and the funds are missing.
A direct debit payment for a utility bill did not go through as scheduled due to a processing error.

themes.name: Banking systems down for hours with no status or fallback
themes.problem_statement: Online banking, the app or the agent's own system is unavailable for hours or days, so the customer cannot log in, pay, deposit or even be helped by phone.
themes.root_cause: Outages and stalled system updates run on with no status page, no fix date and no fallback for customers or for front-line agents.
examples: Your website and app are both down again, which is why I had to call just to find an ATM, and nobody can tell me why it keeps happening.
Customer is unable to access online banking due to an outage, receiving an 'incorrect username' error despite resetting password multiple times.

themes.name: Card declined at pumps and checkout terminals every time
themes.problem_statement: The card is read as an error or not accepted at gas pumps and checkout terminals on every attempt, with funds available and a card that is neither damaged nor expired.
themes.root_cause: Card acceptance fails between the terminal network and the bank and the fault is never traced, so the customer is only told to try somewhere else.
examples: The pump reader says card not accepted every time, although the customer tried another card, checked her balance and inspected the reader for damage.
Every time I use the gas pump at the Main Street station it says card read error, with both my debit and credit cards and at different pumps.

themes.name: Card cannot be added to the phone wallet
themes.problem_statement: Adding the debit card to a phone wallet fails on every attempt with 'card not supported', 'invalid account information' or a bare error, on new phones of both makes.
themes.root_cause: The card tokenisation link to the wallet providers is broken or the card range is not enrolled, and no fix date is given to the customer.
examples: Customer's Union Financial debit card is not supported when trying to set up mobile wallet on a new Samsung Galaxy S21, receiving an error message.
The customer's Union Financial debit card cannot be added to their iPhone 12 mobile wallet because it says 'not supported', due to technical difficulties with the bank's integration.

themes.name: Bill pay rejects a payee whose details are correct
themes.problem_statement: Adding a payee to bill pay returns invalid account or routing information although the customer enters exactly what the biller shows, on both the website and the app.
themes.root_cause: Payee validation runs against a stale or mistyped internal payee record, or against small billers never integrated with bill pay, and the message says only 'incorrect'.
examples: Every time I try to add ABC Electric Company as a payee, bill pay tells me the information I am entering is incorrect.

Adding the electric company as a payee returned invalid account although the details were entered correctly; a typo in the bank's own record was the cause and the agent corrected it and added the payee.

themes.name: New card will not activate and the PIN is refused
themes.problem_statement: Activation fails on the phone system or at the ATM: a PIN the customer never received is demanded, or the PIN they set is rejected, and the card stays unusable.
themes.root_cause: PIN and activation records are missing or wrong when the card ships, so the automated activation path rejects the customer and a manual reset is needed.
examples: The Health Savings Account card did not work because of an issue with its activation; the agent activated it during the call.
An hour of trying to activate the new card failed because the automated system kept asking for a PIN she does not have and the activation code never arrived with the card.

themes.name: One-time code never arrives and no other proof is taken
themes.problem_statement: Access to the account or to a payment is blocked because the one-time code or verification call never arrives, or goes to an old number, and no other proof is accepted.
themes.root_cause: Identity checks hang on one stored phone number that is stale, reassigned or unreachable abroad, and no agent or branch can authorise an alternative proof of identity.
examples: After experiencing fraud and identity theft with money stolen, the account now shows an incorrect phone number that is blocking the customer from accessing her account and funds online.

After a banker verified the customer's identity with state paperwork and moved funds to a newly opened account, $110000.00 in wire transfers were rejected again the next day for the same unresolved identity verification

themes.name: Account locked by a security rule that no one can lift
themes.problem_statement: The account, profile or card is locked, restricted or closed by a security rule with no warning, and calls, verification and branch visits do not lift the block.
themes.root_cause: Automated risk rules lock accounts and hold funds without review, and front-line staff cannot release the restriction, so the block returns after every call.
examples: The account was locked for security and Chase says it can only be unlocked at a branch, but the customer is overseas with no Chase location nearby and can't access funds or pay the Chase credit card.
After the deposit finally showed as available, the debit card was repeatedly declined for both in-person and online transactions.

themes.name: Contact details or cards changed with no check on who asked
themes.problem_statement: A phone number, PIN, address, device or enrolment is added or changed by someone else, or an account is opened in the customer's name, with no verification step at all.
themes.root_cause: Contact and credential changes are accepted on the caller's or applicant's say-so, without being checked against the details already held on the account.
examples: A stranger opened a Chase banking account using the customer's email address, likely due to a typo, and Chase has no email verification step to catch this.
Within two months of opening the account, it was accessed from another region and an unknown person added a phone number to it, leading to three debit cards and repeated lockouts.

themes.name: Fraudulent charges run for months with no alert or block
themes.problem_statement: Unauthorised charges, transfers or duplicate items run for days or months with no alert and no block, while ordinary small purchases still trigger a confirmation.
themes.root_cause: Fraud monitoring misses takeover and duplication patterns, and alerts go to channels the customer may not see, so nothing is raised until they find it themselves.
examples: Before the scam call, the customer had already dealt with multiple unexplained $8.00 charges and two replacement debit cards that were compromised before even being received.
No notice or alert was sent for any of the large unauthorized transfers, even though a much smaller $860.00 purchase triggered a text confirmation request.

themes.name: Charges still post on a card I locked or cancelled
themes.problem_statement: A card the customer locked or cancelled, a charge already declined or a transfer confirmed as cancelled still processes, and the money leaves the account.
themes.root_cause: Locks, cancellations and stop instructions are not passed on to wallet tokens, card-updater networks and payments already in flight, so the old permission still works.
examples: Despite a text confirming a charge was denied and a new card issued, the merchant's retry through a digital wallet let the charge post, resulting in a $34.00 overdraft fee.
Chase gave the customer a document confirming the last hacking-related transfer was canceled, but it went through anyway.

themes.name: Autopay does not collect and I get a late fee
themes.problem_statement: Autopay is set up and confirmed, but the bank never pulls the money, pulls it late or marks it returned, and the customer only finds out from a late fee or a closed account.
themes.root_cause: The standing autopay instruction is dropped, not executed against the funded pay-from account or posted after an internal cutoff, and nothing warns the customer that the collection failed.
examples: The autopay set up for the balance transfer did not deduct as scheduled, so the customer had to pay $150.00 manually the next day.
Autopay was set up but failed to process a credit card payment, possibly due to an app update losing the autopay data, resulting in a first-ever late payment on the account.

themes.name: Transfer sent to the wrong person cannot be recalled
themes.problem_statement: An instant transfer reaches someone the customer never meant to pay, and the bank will not stop, recall or refund it even when it is reported within minutes.
themes.root_cause: The app resolves a saved contact or a mistyped handle without checking who currently owns it and shows no confirmation of the recipient, and sent payments have no stop or recall path.
examples: A glitch in the Chase mobile app sent $35.00 to the wrong recipient, and Chase closed the investigation in under 7 days without a refund.
Payments sent to the wrong person, or needing cancellation, could not be stopped even when reported almost immediately after the transaction.

themes.name: My name or account number is wrong in the bank's records
themes.problem_statement: Payments, bookings, rewards and even finding the account fail because the name or account number the bank holds is reversed, truncated, mis-keyed or out of date.
themes.root_cause: Names and account numbers captured at opening, or reshaped by field length limits and padding rules, are never validated against the customer's real details before other systems use them.
examples: Rewards points transfer to an authorized user's loyalty account, an advertised option, is blocked because Chase's system only accepts last names up to a certain length, and no one warned this would be a problem.
Chase Travel booked a flight using the wife's outdated surname, nearly causing denied boarding, and after hours spent fixing Chase's own error, Chase offered only 50% of the booking cost in points.

themes.name: Settings and instructions revert after being confirmed
themes.problem_statement: A choice the customer makes - the pay-from account, autopay on, paperless off, unsubscribe, a one-off payment - is confirmed and then silently reverts or is applied as something else.
themes.root_cause: Preference and instruction changes are acknowledged at the point of contact but never written to the system of record, so the previous value or a default keeps being applied.
examples: Despite calling multiple times to move autopay from checking to savings, Chase kept charging the old account, bouncing a payment and causing $100.00 in interest that Chase refused to remove or escalate.
Despite receiving confirmation each time that he was unsubscribed from credit card collection emails, he continued receiving them at least ten more times over the following months.

themes.name: Statement and app show wrong balances, rates or points
themes.problem_statement: The app or statement shows a wrong rate, category, balance or points total, or will not show the statement or payment history at all, so the customer cannot see what they owe or earned.
themes.root_cause: Statement, balance and rewards displays are built from records that are not refreshed when rates, categories or postings change, and blocked or missing documents are never regenerated.
examples: A promotional rate that was supposed to expire last week did not update on the statement due to a system issue, causing the customer to be billed at the wrong rate.
An Airbnb reservation was miscategorized as real estate instead of home share, earning far fewer points than the card's advertised home-share bonus rate she has received on other similar stays.

themes.name: Cannot find or finish the task on the website
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot locate the page they need or complete the journey they started: the section is buried, the form demands things they do not have, or the text and links are unusable.
themes.root_cause: Navigation and form journeys ship without anyone checking that a customer can find and finish them end to end, including with low vision or limited dexterity, so they give up and call.
examples: Every time I go to the website all I see are adverts for your products, and I could not find the financial education section.
To book the budgeting and savings workshop I had to create an account, but every password was rejected as too weak and then it asked for a promo code I do not have.

themes.name: App store says my phone is not supported
themes.problem_statement: The app store refuses to install the bank app, reporting the phone as unsupported, and the customer is left with no working app on the device they already own.
themes.root_cause: The published app supports a device and OS range that lags behind what customers carry, new releases are not certified quickly, and no alternative access is offered meanwhile.
examples: The App Store kept saying the app was not compatible with the customer's iPhone 8 on iOS 14.2, and restarting the device and retrying several times did not help.
I keep getting an error message trying to download and use the mobile app, and it turns out the app only works on Android devices, not my iPhone.

themes.name: Locked out of accounts and tabs my profile should reach
themes.problem_statement: A tab, an account or a report is refused as access denied or locked although colleagues in the same role can reach it, and no agent can change what the profile is allowed to see.
themes.root_cause: Entitlements on business and investment profiles are provisioned wrongly at setup and can only be changed by a back-office team the front line has no route to.
examples: The customer wants to move funds into a different mutual fund but the website will not let him into his locked retirement account to make the change.
I get an error saying I do not have enough clearance when I try to view our company's financial statements, while a colleague in the same role can see them.

themes.name: App crashes, freezes or takes an age to load
themes.problem_statement: The app or online banking platform crashes, freezes or takes an age to load, often right after login, for weeks and on more than one device.
themes.root_cause: App releases ship without stability and performance testing on the devices customers actually carry, and crash reports are not tied to a fix or a release date.
examples: Several download attempts end in an error message and, when the customer does manage to log in, the app crashes; this has gone on for weeks despite a password reset and a different device.
The online banking platform takes forever to load and sometimes freezes up completely after a week of trying to use the new services.

themes.name: other: fraud_not_stopped_or_not_refunded
themes.problem_statement: Statements about fraud not stopped or not refunded that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Checks I never wrote were paid from my account
themes.problem_statement: Forged checks drawn on the customer's account number are paid in full, and the customer only finds out from a statement, a letter or a collections agency.
themes.root_cause: Nothing verifies the signature or the issuing pattern before a check is paid, so the money only gets chased once the customer reports it.
examples: Someone has been writing bad checks with my account information, and I only found out when a collections agency chased me for a check I never wrote.
Several checks the customer did not write, made out to different people and adding up to a significant amount, were cashed against her checking account within the last week.

themes.name: Unauthorised payments found by me, not stopped by the bank
themes.problem_statement: Transactions the customer never authorised post to the account, are spotted by the customer rather than the bank, and the money stays gone while a dispute runs.
themes.root_cause: Fraud monitoring does not stop or alert on these payments, and any refund waits on a manual dispute form and investigation before anything is reversed.
examples: Several suspicious transactions were made on the customer's account over the past few days; he authorised none of them and only found most of them on his statement.
I noticed a few transactions I did not make and believe someone accessed my account and made purchases without my knowledge.

themes.name: Unauthorised recurring debits the bank will not cancel
themes.problem_statement: Recurring or pre-authorised debits set up by a third party the customer never dealt with keep coming out, and the bank says it cannot cancel or refund them.
themes.root_cause: Nothing checks that the customer authorised the mandate, and stopping a third-party debit is treated as the merchant's job rather than the bank's.
examples: I did not authorise the payment and I do not recognise the company it was paid to, and it cannot simply be cancelled now.
Pre-authorized debits for a monthly subscription were set up on my account by a company called Easy Pay that I have never heard of and never authorised.

themes.name: Elder exploitation reported by family cannot be acted on
themes.problem_statement: A relative reports withdrawals and transfers an elderly, confused account holder could not have made, and the bank cannot act without her own authorisation.
themes.root_cause: There is no route to act on a third party's report of financial exploitation, so a vulnerable customer's account keeps paying out.
examples: My mother is in her eighties, has become forgetful and confused, and her statement shows large withdrawals she could not possibly have made herself.
The customer's mother-in-law is getting calls and emails from people posing as the bank asking her to verify account information, and suspicious transactions have already shown up.

themes.name: Impersonation of the bank is only logged, never stopped
themes.problem_statement: Emails and calls impersonating the bank reach the customer asking for account details, and the bank can only record and monitor rather than stop them.
themes.root_cause: No takedown or outbound warning follows an impersonation report, so the burden of spotting the fake sits entirely on the customer.
examples: I got two emails yesterday that looked like they were from the bank, one asking me to click a link to update my account information and one asking for my personal information.
Two emails from what looked like the bank's own address asked me to update my account information with my social security number and to click a link about a problem with my account.

themes.name: they say my PIN was used, so it must have been me
themes.problem_statement: A fraud claim is denied, or a credit reversed, because a PIN, chip, biometric or the customer's own details were used - even with a police report, video, or the card still in hand.
themes.root_cause: Authentication data is treated as conclusive proof that the customer authorised the payment, so the investigation stops there and the evidence of theft is never weighed.
examples: Money forced out at an ATM by armed robbers, with a police report filed, was denied a refund because Chase said entering the PIN under duress disqualifies reimbursement until suspects are prosecuted.

An identity thief who ordered a replacement debit card and set her own PIN spent $1600.00 in debit card purchases that Chase still calls authorized, despite video evidence of her picking up the card and a filed police re

themes.name: Temporary refund clawed back without explanation
themes.problem_statement: A temporary credit for the disputed amount is paid, then clawed back days or weeks later, often leaving the account negative and the customer with no explanation of the change.
themes.root_cause: Provisional credit is issued before any real investigation, and the later review reverses it on the merchant's word, with the reasoning never shared with the customer.
examples: After a phone and wallet theft abroad led to $870.00 in fraudulent ATM, purchase and transfer transactions, Chase issued a temporary credit but then withdrew it days later after review.

Two unauthorized debit charges totaling $960.00 were reversed and then charged back because the merchandise was 'received,' even though a thief simply printed the invoice and picked it up in person without ever showing I

themes.name: Fraud claim denied despite the evidence I provided
themes.problem_statement: Police reports, video, written admissions and the bank's own findings are handed in with the claim, yet it is denied, part-paid or closed with no explanation and no way to reopen it.
themes.root_cause: Claims are decided on merchant and internal data alone, with no step to weigh the customer's evidence and no reasoned decision, so denials repeat on new grounds each time.
examples: A $9,400.00 fraud claim confirmed by XXXX was denied twice by Chase, both times citing prior authorized transactions with the same vendor despite evidence of fraud.
$10,000.00 was taken through transactions at Chase branches in NJ and Washington that the customer never visited, and both fraud claims filed were closed with no refund.

themes.name: Money I was tricked into sending is treated as authorised
themes.problem_statement: A scammer, often posing as the bank's own fraud team, walks the customer through a wire, a Zelle payment or gift cards, and the bank calls it authorised and will not try to recover it.
themes.root_cause: Payments the customer was tricked into making are treated as authorised, so there is no recall, no reimbursement route and no warning at the moment of an out-of-character transfer.
examples: A caller posing as Chase's Fraud Department convinced the customer to send a transfer to 'reverse' a supposed unauthorized transaction, and the $750.00 never came back.

A $3,700.00 check from a dog-sitting job scam was deposited, and $3,200.00 was wired per the scammer's request before the customer grew suspicious; the branch said the funds probably cannot be recovered.

themes.name: More fraud goes through after I reported it
themes.problem_statement: More unauthorised transactions, transfers or withdrawals go through after the customer reported the fraud, was issued a new card, or was told the account had been frozen.
themes.root_cause: Reporting fraud does not actually block the account or the items already in flight, so wallets, pending payments and open channels keep paying out after the freeze.
examples: More unauthorized charges came through even after the claim was filed and new debit cards were issued.
After reporting fraud and asking Chase to freeze the account, two more identical $2000.00 unauthorized transfers to the same recipient still went through.

themes.name: Stolen money sits in an account at the same bank, untouched
themes.problem_statement: The victim can show the money landed in another account at the same bank, but it is not frozen, investigated or recovered because the victim does not own that account.
themes.root_cause: There is no route for a victim to have a receiving account acted on, so the funds keep moving while the bank treats its own account holder's activity as nothing to do with them.
examples: Family members allegedly stole a large sum of cash from her home and deposited it into accounts at Chase and other banks, and she wants the money returned and accounts blocked.

An employee transferred over $1,000,000 from company accounts into shell companies and a personal account at Chase, and Chase continued processing suspicious transactions for months after being notified of the embezzleme

themes.name: Account opened in my name and not closed on request
themes.problem_statement: An account, or a business linked to one, that the customer never applied for is opened with their stolen details, and closing it is refused or demands more personal data.
themes.root_cause: New applications are not matched against the real owner of the identity used, and there is no clean route to close an account that was opened fraudulently.
examples: Chase opened a checking account using the customer's name, address and email without any request, and refuses to close the fraudulent account unless the customer provides their Social Security number.
Several other accounts were opened in her name by the thief without her knowledge, and she wants them removed from her credit.

themes.name: Fake check accepted on deposit and the loss passed to me
themes.problem_statement: A forged, altered or stolen check is deposited into an account it does not belong to, or into the customer's account by a fraudster, and the customer carries the returned amount.
themes.root_cause: Deposits are accepted without verifying the payee, the endorsement or the item itself, and the loss is passed back to the account holder once the check is returned.
examples: A loan scammer gained remote access to the account and deposited a fake check via mobile deposit without permission, and Chase later insisted the check was genuinely the customer's.
Instead of depositing a promised loan via ACH, a loan company logged into her Chase account without authorization and made a mobile deposit of a fake check.

themes.name: an imposter passed your ID checks and was served as me
themes.problem_statement: An imposter using a fake ID, a stolen phone or only a phone call is handed cash, a bank check, a replacement card or an address change on the customer's account.
themes.root_cause: Branch and phone identity checks are not enforced or evidenced, so a card, a PIN or a plausible story is enough to be served as the account holder.
examples: The imposter made 42 unauthorized transactions totaling $17,000.00 using the replacement card, and Chase denied all the fraud claims.
A thief using a fake ID withdrew $7,000 cash and a $28,000 bank check, then returned to withdraw another $8,000, and the money has not been returned.

themes.name: my account was closed instead of the fraud investigated
themes.problem_statement: After fraud is reported the account is frozen, restricted or closed and the balance held or clawed back, so the victim loses their banking as well as the stolen money.
themes.root_cause: Fraud handling defaults to ending the relationship rather than investigating it, and nobody owns reinstating the customer or explaining the decision.
examples: In 2021, Chase froze the account over an accusation of scamming another member and said the money would go to that person, while unexplained charges from a state never visited also drained funds, and none of it was ever
Disputed amounts from Cash App and Chase were never refunded, and the accounts were closed abruptly with no help or explanation given.

themes.name: fraud claim refused because the 60-day window had passed
themes.problem_statement: A fraud claim is refused, or accepted only in part, because a 60-day or similar window has run out, though the customer reported it as soon as they could have seen it.
themes.root_cause: The dispute clock runs from when each item posted rather than from when the customer could reasonably have noticed it, with no exception where the bank's own monitoring missed the pattern.
examples: Unauthorized recurring debits totaling $18,000.00 over two years went undetected due to their gradual escalation, and Chase only permitted disputes for a portion of them.
A $2000.00 rent check was fraudulently altered and rewritten to a different payee, but the claim was denied because more than 60 days had passed since the incident.

themes.name: the temporary credit promised on my claim never arrived
themes.problem_statement: The customer is told a temporary or partial credit will post within days while the claim is reviewed; it never arrives, with no denial, no explanation and nobody to chase.
themes.root_cause: Provisional credit is promised when the claim is taken but nothing books it or tracks the deadline, so the promise dies with the call while the customer stays out of pocket.
examples: Unauthorized debit card charges to a North Carolina rental company and a Virginia-based merchant left the checking account fully withdrawn, and no promised credit for the stolen amount was ever issued.
Over $2,100.00 in ATM withdrawals and merchandise purchases were made using a stolen debit card and PIN, and the temporary credit Chase promised while reviewing the claim was never issued.

themes.name: my stolen reward points were never put back
themes.problem_statement: Reward points are redeemed by a fraudster during an account compromise and are never restored, even when the cash charges from the same incident are refunded.
themes.root_cause: Loyalty points sit outside the fraud reimbursement process, so a claim is settled on the dollar amounts with nobody owning reinstatement of the points.
examples: Reward points were used without authorization for a $62.00 purchase on an account that wasn't the customer's; the $62.00 was refunded quickly but the stolen points have not been returned.
Reward points from two long-held credit cards were redeemed for gift cards at the same time as other fraudulent transactions, but Chase concluded the customer benefited and took no further action.

themes.name: the account opened in my name is still on my credit file
themes.problem_statement: An account or inquiry the customer never authorised keeps being reported to the credit bureaus and chased by collectors long after identity theft was reported with paperwork.
themes.root_cause: Closing a fraudulent account and stopping the reporting of it are separate steps, and nothing acts on an identity theft affidavit to block the tradeline at the bureaus.
examples: My credit report lists two accounts I do not recognise, from XYZ Bank and ABC Credit Card Company, and the bank confirmed both were opened fraudulently with my information.
A credit card statement arrived for an account I never opened, and my credit report shows several other accounts I do not recognise.

themes.name: neither the bank nor the payment app will refund the fraud
themes.problem_statement: Money lost through a transfer service, payment app or marketplace is reported to both the bank and the platform, and each says the other must handle it or that the rail is not covered.
themes.root_cause: Fraud on a third-party payment rail sits outside the bank's dispute process and nobody owns the claim end to end, so the customer is passed between the two.
examples: $900.00 sent to a scam concert ticket seller through a peer-to-peer payment app was never returned, and both the bank and the app said they could not reverse the payment.
A $200 payment sent to a marketplace scammer could not be recovered because the bank and the payment app each redirected her to the other.

themes.name: my payment went out without checking the payee's name
themes.problem_statement: Money is released to an account that is not the payee the customer meant to pay, because the recipient's name or details are never confirmed before the transfer leaves.
themes.root_cause: No step matches the payee name to the receiving account before a transfer is released, so a swapped contact or a mismatched beneficiary is paid anyway.
examples: A $220.00 Zelle payment meant for the customer's sister went to an unknown recipient because there was no confirmation step, and it was not treated as fraud.
An $18,000.00 wire was credited to a scammer's Chase account despite a name mismatch Chase acknowledged violated verification practices, and the funds were never returned.

themes.name: a fake profile in my name and nobody will take it down
themes.problem_statement: An impersonation profile in the customer's name posts as them or asks their contacts for money, and neither the bank nor the platform removes it after it is reported.
themes.root_cause: Impersonation outside the bank's own systems has no owner and no takedown route, so the fake profile stays up and the customer is left to chase the platform.
examples: Someone is posing as the customer on Facebook, posting fraudulent information, and trying to get friends to send them money.
Someone is posing as the customer on Facebook, posting strange things and messaging people for money, and the bank says it cannot do anything about it.

themes.name: other: policy_or_terms_change
themes.problem_statement: Statements about policy or terms change that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: my savings rate was lowered and nobody told me
themes.problem_statement: The rate on a savings account or CD drops with the market or at renewal and the customer only finds out from a statement, a letter or this call.
themes.root_cause: Rates are repriced automatically against the benchmark or at rollover and the change notice is not sent, or does not reach the customer before the new rate applies.
examples: The interest rate on my variable rate savings account went down, and I thought these accounts were supposed to earn more over time, not less.
The customer's interest rate fell last month because the benchmark moved, and she feels she should be earning more, not less, on her savings.

themes.name: my promotional rate ended with no renewal offered
themes.problem_statement: The promotional savings rate the customer opened the account for ends on its term date, and no extension, renewal or comparable offer is available.
themes.root_cause: Promotions are tied to a fixed end date with no successor offer or retention path for existing customers, and the expiry letter arrives without options.
examples: The promotional interest rate on the savings account expired, and after receiving the letter the customer hoped it could be extended but was told promotions cannot be renewed.
A letter said my savings promotional interest rate had expired last month, and the bank said the promotion cannot be extended any further.

themes.name: a new or higher fee I only found out about after paying it
themes.problem_statement: A monthly, overdraft or service fee is introduced or raised and the customer discovers it from the statement, from online banking or on this call, often after paying it.
themes.root_cause: Fee and eligibility changes are published through statement inserts or website updates instead of a direct notice the customer has to acknowledge.
examples: Chase requires auto loan payments 3 business days before a due date that falls on a Sunday or be penalized, a policy the customer says isn't clearly disclosed.

When the lease payment due date falls on a weekend, Chase requires the funds to be available before the due date rather than the next business day after, a requirement not stated in the signed lease contract.

themes.name: a simple request needs a branch visit or a paper form
themes.problem_statement: Simple account requests cannot be completed by phone or online, so the customer must travel to a branch or send faxed or notarised paper forms.
themes.root_cause: Signature and identity rules exclude the phone and digital channels for account maintenance, with no remote verification route for customers who cannot travel.
examples: Bank policy requires a faxed request for a loan payoff amount, which cannot be provided over the phone or online and takes 24-48 hours to process.
Customer needs a copy of last month's bank statement but the bank's security policy prevents emailing it, requiring an in-person branch visit.

themes.name: account frozen or closed with no reason given
themes.problem_statement: Accounts are restricted, locked or closed without advance notice, blocking deposits and access to funds, and no branch or phone staff will explain why.
themes.root_cause: Risk and compliance decisions are executed centrally with no customer notice, and front-line staff are barred from disclosing the reason behind them.
examples: The checking account was closed without prior notification, blocking a paycheck deposit and causing the customer to fall behind on rent.
Chase closed the checking account without authorization, further complicating the ability to get information about the refund status.

themes.name: credit limit changed with no notice and no explanation
themes.problem_statement: The credit limit is cut overnight, often to the exact balance, or raised without being asked - no warning, no explanation anyone will give, and a credit score that drops with it.
themes.root_cause: Automated portfolio reviews reprice limits on balance and bureau data alone, and the decision reaches the customer with no notice, no reasoning and no route to appeal it.
examples: The credit limit on the Amazon Chase card was reduced to an unusable level while a billing-error arbitration and a dispute affidavit were still pending and unrebutted.
A credit limit was cut by a large amount overnight with no justification, tanking the credit score, despite over two decades of on-time, above-minimum payments.

themes.name: reward points wiped out when the card was closed
themes.problem_statement: Rewards points built up over years are forfeited the moment the account is closed, downgraded or shut for inactivity, with no warning and no chance to redeem or move them first.
themes.root_cause: Point forfeiture runs automatically on closure and the closure notice never mentions it, even where the programme is sold as one currency shared across the customer's accounts.
examples: Closing a single Chase credit card resulted in the forfeiture of accumulated Ultimate Rewards points, without any disclosure during the closure call that this would happen.
Chase closed the account without direct email or mail notice, instead posting the closure notice six clicks deep in an online portal section, causing forfeiture of over $1400.00 in rewards points.

themes.name: the advertised bonus or benefit is not the one honoured
themes.problem_statement: An advertised bonus, statement credit or card benefit is refused, shrunk or narrowed after the fact, with the bank citing conditions the customer was never shown.
themes.root_cause: The offer as marketed and the terms actually booked on the account live in different systems, and later changes to benefits are applied without notifying the customer.
examples: The credit card that arrived did not include the advertised $200.00 statement credit and carried a $69.00 annual fee despite being advertised with no annual fee.
Chase said a purchase could not earn both the 5% quarterly category bonus and 3% Shop through Chase reward, but this exclusion was not advertised anywhere.

themes.name: interest rate raised with no notice and no explanation
themes.problem_statement: The APR on a card is raised, or interest starts accruing under a rule such as a lost grace period, with no notice beforehand and no explanation when the customer asks for one.
themes.root_cause: Repricing and interest rules are applied at portfolio level and the change notice is never sent or is buried, so the first sign is a larger interest charge on the statement.
examples: I got a notice that the APR on my credit card is going up, which means more interest on my balance, and it does not seem fair.
After the interest charges were waived, a supervisor said that going forward, any new purchase will accrue interest as long as the balance transfer balance remains, even if paid off monthly.

themes.name: blocked by an internal rule that was never disclosed
themes.problem_statement: A hold, cut-off, restriction or enrolment the customer was never told about blocks a payment, a purchase or access to their own money, and appears only in the bank's internal rules.
themes.root_cause: Risk and processing rules sit outside the published terms, so staff can only state them after they bite and the customer has no way to plan around them.
examples: A withdrawal was denied by the branch manager under a 'business day' rule that aggregates weekend days into Monday's limit, a rule never fully disclosed to the customer.
A policy limiting fee refunds to once a year left most of the over $500.00 in overdraft fees charged over two years unrefunded, even when the customer believed the fees were caused by posting delays.

themes.name: rate reset raises a payment the customer thought was fixed
themes.problem_statement: The payment on a mortgage or loan rises when the index resets, and the customer believed the rate was fixed or capped and was never told how far it could actually move.
themes.root_cause: Adjustable products are sold without the reset mechanics being understood or restated before the first adjustment, and no cap, freeze or refinance option is offered when it bites.
examples: The rate on the Adjustable-Rate Mortgage moved from 3.75% to 4.25%, so the payment increased sharply this month, and the customer thought a cap limited the increase.
The rate on the customer's ARM is going up because the LIBOR index rose, taking the monthly payment to $1,025, quite a bit higher than she pays now, and nothing can stop it.

themes.name: new outside rules add fees and the bank says it cannot help
themes.problem_statement: New regulations or tariffs add fees, extra verification steps or outright rejections to the customer's transactions, and the bank says it has no control and can do nothing.
themes.root_cause: Externally driven rule changes are passed straight through to customers with no advance warning, no workaround offered and no route to have the impact reviewed.
examples: I am being charged more for the same international transactions I have been making for years, and nobody has explained why the tariff changes hit my account.
Payments to the customer's supplier in China keep being rejected because the beneficiary's bank cannot receive them under the new tariffs, and the supplier needs paying urgently.

themes.name: no service without giving a Social Security number by phone
themes.problem_statement: A wire, a new account or even a general question is refused because the customer will not give a Social Security number or other personal details over the phone.
themes.root_cause: Identity and account-opening rules accept only one set of personal data, with no alternative proof for customers who are unwilling to give it over the phone.
examples: Customer cannot complete a wire transfer because they are unwilling to provide their Social Security Number over the phone for verification, as required by bank policy.
The customer was uncomfortable sharing their Social Security Number over the phone for identity verification, which prevented the agent from accessing the account and providing personalized advice.

themes.name: no affordable payment plan offered after income drops
themes.problem_statement: After a job loss or a drop in income the customer asks for a modification or a plan they can afford, and only a system-set payment, or nothing at all, is offered.
themes.root_cause: Hardship terms are generated by a scoring system with no room to match the customer's real income, and nobody can override the offer before arrears are reported.
examples: Customer is two months behind on mortgage payments due to job loss and is seeking options like a loan modification to reduce monthly payments.
During a government-shutdown-caused job loss, no affordable payment option was offered, resulting in late payment reporting that is now hurting the credit score and access to financing.

themes.name: escrow reanalysis suddenly raises the monthly payment
themes.problem_statement: The monthly mortgage payment rises sharply because escrow was re-analysed, set up unilaterally or left to build a shortage, and the customer only hears about it afterwards.
themes.root_cause: Escrow reanalysis is run late or an escrow account is opened without agreement after a tax, insurance or payment change, so the shortage compounds before the new payment lands.
examples: Nobody told me about the property tax increase before my payment changed, and the agent could only suggest the county notice may have gone astray.
After failing to collect my mortgage payment twice, Chase diverted part of a $970.00 payment into an escrow account it unilaterally established, then raised my payment to over $1,100.00.

themes.name: other: staff_attitude_or_competence
themes.problem_statement: Statements about staff attitude or competence that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: staff are rude or impatient with a routine request
themes.problem_statement: Tellers and phone agents give no greeting, act annoyed at questions, rush the transaction or leave the customer feeling like a nuisance.
themes.root_cause: No enforced service standard or coaching on tone at the counter and on the phone, with queue and handling-time pressure rewarded over the interaction itself.
examples: Representatives were rude, interrupted repeatedly, and refused to take a delivery tracking number that would have helped locate the payoff check.
I went into the Main Street branch last week to open a checking account and the representative was unfriendly and seemed annoyed when I asked her to explain the options.

themes.name: the agent does not know how to handle the request
themes.problem_statement: The agent taking the call cannot handle or does not understand the request, gives no answer and no follow-up, so the customer has to call again about the same thing.
themes.root_cause: Front-line staff are not trained or equipped for specialist requests such as estates, custodial accounts or new services, and nobody owns an unfinished case.
examples: I was transferred to technical support, who were no help at all, and I was left to go into a branch instead.
The first agent said she could not assist with access levels and could not escalate the request, so the customer had to ask to be transferred.

themes.name: a fraud or dispute report is met with blame, not help
themes.problem_statement: Customers reporting fraud, a scam or a disputed charge are told it is their own fault or bad luck, treated as suspects and refused the evidence behind a denial.
themes.root_cause: Claims and fraud teams work to denial scripts with no duty to share evidence or explain the decision, so the customer hears blame instead of an investigation.
examples: One representative told me the fraud was not the bank's problem and that I should deal with the police and the collections agency myself.
After reporting the scam, representatives told the customer it was 'too bad for your bad luck' and that nothing could be done.

themes.name: escalation ends with no supervisor and no callback
themes.problem_statement: A request for a supervisor ends in a long wait, a dismissive manager, a dropped call or a logged complaint, and the promised callback never comes.
themes.root_cause: The escalation path has no authority to make exceptions and no tracked callback commitment, so escalations close as documented concerns rather than actions.
examples: Requesting a supervisor meant a three-day wait with no callback received, and every attempt to resolve the issue was met with a refusal to extend the payment deadline.
Two Chase representatives disconnected the call while the customer was trying to resolve the title delay.

themes.name: ID checks demand details the request does not need
themes.problem_statement: Before anything can be done the customer is asked for a social security number, employer, login details or documents that have nothing to do with the question.
themes.root_cause: A scripted identity check collects a fixed set of fields whatever the request, and agents cannot proceed when the customer declines or the records do not match.
examples: She was told she was eligible for the automatic savings plan but the agent would not complete it, handing her another department's phone number after she declined to give her social security number.
The first agent kept asking for information that was not necessary and did not seem to understand my situation, which made the call far longer than it needed to be.

themes.name: Accused of fraud and refused my own verified money
themes.problem_statement: Staff refuse to cash, deposit or release the customer's own verified money, accuse them of fraud in front of others and threaten arrest, trespass or the police.
themes.root_cause: Branch and phone staff act on a personal suspicion flag with no evidence test and no manager review, and are backed by policy that lets them refuse service without explaining why.
examples: A branch representative was very rude, accused the customer of criminal activity, and threatened that they could be arrested.
A branch manager refused to accept a valid California mobile driver's license for a withdrawal, refused to give her name, and threatened to call the police when asked for policy documentation.

themes.name: No staff name, case number or decision in writing
themes.problem_statement: Staff refuse to give their name or employee ID, a claim or complaint reference, a written breakdown or the documents behind a decision, leaving the customer nothing to act on.
themes.root_cause: No requirement to identify the handler or issue a written record of a decision, so agents can close a call without leaving any trace the customer can use to escalate.
examples: A phone representative added some fee compensation but was dismissive about the unauthorized account change, refused to provide documentation of any notice, and denied escalation to a manager.
Repeated requests for a written breakdown or confirmation of the reversal were denied, and the customer was hung up on and dismissed.

themes.name: Account closed or frozen after I pushed back on staff
themes.problem_statement: Soon after the customer complains, pushes back or has an awkward exchange with an employee, the account is restricted, closed or flagged, with no contestable reason given.
themes.root_cause: Branch and fraud staff can flag or close an account on their own read of the customer, with no independent review of the decision and no written reason the customer can challenge.
examples: The customer's account was closed for being 'rude to employees,' which she believes was retaliation for sending a demand letter to executives and threatening legal action after months of unhelpful, dismissive service.
The customer was ignored at a branch while another customer was served first, and after raising the concern, the accounts were closed without warning.

themes.name: Service refused or worsened over my background or name
themes.problem_statement: The customer is questioned about visa status, background or name, misgendered, or told staff are uncomfortable serving 'someone like me', and service worsens from that point.
themes.root_cause: Discretionary suspicion at the counter and in security screening is unmonitored for bias, with no fair-treatment check on refusals, closures or extra questioning.
examples: A security call center representative was rude when the customer explained his background, and his son's account was closed the next day, leading him to believe Chase profiles by name.

A branch agent refused to release confirmed legitimate funds, saying they were uncomfortable giving it to 'someone like me,' and called the police even though the customer had not been asked to leave.

themes.name: Staff booked my transaction wrong and denied the error
themes.problem_statement: A teller or banker deposits to the wrong account, ignores an explicit instruction or changes details without authorisation, then denies the mistake or leaves the customer to undo it.
themes.root_cause: No read-back or maker-checker on counter and phone transactions and no route for staff to reverse their own error, so denying it is easier than correcting it.
examples: A banker placed the deposit into savings instead of the requested checking account and asked personal questions unrelated to the transaction.
The same day I visited the branch, someone there changed my son's account information without either of our authorization, which he had to reverse himself.

themes.name: Hung up on mid-request, with no callback
themes.problem_statement: The agent hangs up, disconnects or transfers the customer to an unattended line while they are still explaining, and nobody calls back.
themes.root_cause: Ending a call carries no consequence: disconnects are not tracked per agent and there is no duty to call back a case that was cut off.
examples: The earlier call about the rewards program ended with what the customer describes as the representative hanging up on him.
A U.S.-based representative hung up on the customer, saying their unprofessional demeanor invalidated their privilege to receive customer service.

themes.name: Threatening collection calls that do not stop when asked
themes.problem_statement: Collection calls continue day and night, to family, employer and colleagues, after requests to stop, with threats of arrest, a sheriff or a home visit.
themes.root_cause: Dialler lists and outside agencies are not stopped by a cease-and-desist or hardship flag, and collection scripts are not monitored for threats or contact limits.
examples: Chase called repeatedly day and night for payment during a financial hardship and would not accept a reduced payment amount she offered.
The company kept calling and bothering the customer during hospitalization despite being told payment would come at release, then canceled the account after the first payment was made.

themes.name: Reconsideration offered only via another hard credit pull
themes.problem_statement: To reconsider a limit cut, a denial or a pre-check, staff offer only a new hard inquiry, which the customer is told will change nothing but will hurt their credit.
themes.root_cause: Staff have no soft pre-qualification or internal review route, so a fresh bureau pull is the only action the system allows them on a credit decision.
examples: A branch specialist pressured the customer into a credit inquiry despite wanting to avoid one without a pre-approval, and the recommended card was then denied.
When asking for reconsideration, Chase's only offer was another hard credit pull, which the representative admitted would show nothing different from days earlier.

themes.name: Sold a product instead of the advice I asked for
themes.problem_statement: The customer asks for guidance on investments, a loan or a product and is pushed something they never asked for, or given no reasoned recommendation at all.
themes.root_cause: Branch and advisory staff are measured on what they sell and have no duty to give or record a recommendation fitted to the customer's goals, so a pitch takes the place of advice.
examples: I have been with you for a while and I do not feel I am getting the best advice or the personalized service I deserve.
The customer wanted guidance on giving in a tax-efficient way and on how her money would be used, but got no real recommendation and ended the call without taking anything up.

themes.name: Repeating my details and story at every transfer
themes.problem_statement: The customer repeats their identity, their account number and their whole story after every hold, transfer and new call, and staff still cannot find the account they hold.
themes.root_cause: Nothing carries the verified caller, the notes and the reason for the call across holds, transfers and repeat calls, and account search fails on the details the customer gives.
examples: After taking all my details the agent said she was still training and had no access to claims, so I had to be transferred.
After the hold the agent asked me what I needed again, so I had to repeat that I wanted a banker's appointment.

themes.name: other: repeated_contact_needed
themes.problem_statement: Statements about repeated contact needed that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: no record of the first call, so it all starts again
themes.problem_statement: The earlier call about the same request produced no answer and no action, so the customer calls again and explains the whole thing from the start.
themes.root_cause: No case is raised and nobody owns an unfinished request, so every call begins again with an agent who may not know the process either.
examples: Customer had to call again because the loan payoff amount was not provided during a previous call last week.
My earlier call got disconnected and the person before would not give me the balance over the phone, even though my dad passed away last month.

themes.name: given another number to call because no transfer is possible
themes.problem_statement: The agent cannot do what is needed and cannot transfer the call, so the customer is given another number and has to start all over again themselves.
themes.root_cause: Departments are reachable only on their own lines, and front-line agents have neither transfer capability nor direct numbers they are allowed to give out.
examples: The customer called to renew his certificate of deposit, but after several verification attempts the agent could not locate the account and the department had no access to CD information.
Offered a transfer to another department, the customer refused because she did not want to be transferred again, and gave up on the call altogether.

themes.name: transferred for lack of authority and made to start again
themes.problem_statement: The first agent lacks the access or authority to act, transfers the call, and the customer repeats the identity check and the entire story to the next team.
themes.root_cause: Transfers carry no case context or verification state, and first-line permissions are too narrow for common requests such as account changes and disputes.
examples: The phone agent could not open the account himself and transferred me again to customer care, so I had to repeat everything after the branch visit.
The initial agent was unable to assist with the account transition and had to transfer the customer to the Account Management team.

themes.name: identity verification repeated at every call and handover
themes.problem_statement: The details the customer gives are rejected, or demanded again after verifying on an earlier call or with the previous agent, so the actual request is never reached.
themes.root_cause: Verification is re-run per call and per department against records that are stale or mismatched, with no way to carry a verified session across the handover.
examples: The customer experienced a frustrating and prolonged identity verification process, requiring account number, social security number, and an online driver's license upload.
A new debit card PIN took two rounds of identity verification and a transfer to a separate PIN reset department before a random PIN was generated.

themes.name: a long call ends with a required trip to the branch
themes.problem_statement: After a long call the customer is told the matter can only be handled in person, and must travel to a branch with documents for something started by phone.
themes.root_cause: Card, dispute and account-change processes have no remote completion path, and the phone line and the branch each say the other one has to handle it.
examples: The customer already called last week and spoke to John, who could not help either, and she now has to take identification to a branch in person.
After the reset failed the customer was told the problem needs personal attention at a branch, so he has to go in tomorrow instead of it being fixed on the call.

themes.name: the call drops on transfer and nobody rings back
themes.problem_statement: The call is cut off mid-request or during a transfer, and because nobody rings back the customer redials and repeats the verification and the whole story to a new agent.
themes.root_cause: Transfers drop calls and no callback number or case note is taken before the handover, so a disconnection wipes out everything done on the call.
examples: An earlier call about this got disconnected, and every time I call about the loan I am transferred to someone new who does not seem to know what is going on.
The joint account setup was never completed, and after a disconnected earlier call he had to go through account number, social security number, address and date of birth again.

themes.name: customer made to gather the proof for a bank-side error
themes.problem_statement: To get a bank-side problem fixed the customer is told to gather the evidence themselves: file a police report, email or fax receipts, or take it up with an outside body.
themes.root_cause: Remediation processes place the burden of proof and of contacting third parties on the customer, because staff have no mandate to investigate or act on the bank's own records.
examples: To fix the bank's own technical error I have to verify the missing transactions and send the receipts in by email or fax myself.
The card cannot be cancelled and reissued until the customer files a police report and brings it into a branch, which she felt was unfair when the bank's security failed.

themes.name: self-service does not work, so every step needs a call
themes.problem_statement: The online form, the payment screen or the self-service route is confusing or broken, and the information is never sent in writing, so the customer has to ring again for each step.
themes.root_cause: Digital journeys are incomplete or fail silently and routine information is released only after a phone verification, so the call centre is the only working channel.
examples: I do not see why I have to keep calling for this information instead of the bank simply sending me a statement about my coverage.
The online application form for the new checking account was confusing and I had to call customer service twice to get my questions answered.

themes.name: already-sent documents demanded again, restarting the clock
themes.problem_statement: Evidence already sent in - receipts, police reports, notarised declarations - is called missing or asked for again, and each round restarts the review timeline.
themes.root_cause: Documents are attached to a call rather than to the case and receipt is never confirmed, so each reviewer sees an incomplete file and reopens the clock.
examples: Chase forced the customer to resubmit disputes multiple times instead of processing the original claim, appearing to reset the Regulation E investigation deadline.
Chase demanded phone, ID, and reissue verification for an endorsed check over several months, rejected each one, then closed the account without permission and never released the money.

themes.name: no case owner and no way to reach whoever decides
themes.problem_statement: Months or years of calls, branch visits and refused escalations, while the decision sits with a back office, security team or executive office nobody can speak to.
