themes.root_cause: Back-office decision teams have no customer contact route and no named case owner, and front-line escalation ends in a note rather than an accountable handover.
examples: The case has dragged on far past an initial two-week estimate, with nobody held accountable despite the customer's long banking history.
The customer cannot speak with the person who decided the fraud claim and keeps getting redirected without resolution despite decades as a Chase customer.

themes.name: collection calls continue after the debt is settled
themes.problem_statement: The customer is called again and again, sometimes several times an hour, about a debt that is settled, dissolved or already dealt with, and confirmations that the record was updated change nothing.
themes.root_cause: The dialler works from a list that account updates, estate notices, bankruptcy filings and payment arrangements never reach, so nothing noted on the account stops the calls.
examples: I am sick of being harassed by collections, who started calling nonstop after my business struggled and I fell behind on bills.
A 40% settlement offer made before the due date was met with no guarantee and instructions to call back later, and the company is now repeatedly calling and emailing without negotiating.

themes.name: an agreed preference reverts and must be asked for again
themes.problem_statement: A preference the customer has already agreed - no escrow account, a different payment date - is not kept, so the same request has to be made again every month or every year.
themes.root_cause: The change is applied as a one-off on the account instead of stored as a standing preference, so the routine process reverts it and nobody records the earlier instruction.
examples: For the third time in as many years, Chase is trying to set up an escrow account on the mortgage to collect for insurance that is already paid directly.
I have to ask for my loan due date to be moved from the 15th to the 20th every single month because the system will not make it automatic.

themes.name: no specialist available and no appointment can be booked
themes.problem_statement: The customer calls again and again to speak to an advisor or specialist, and is told none are available, with no date offered and no way to book or be called back.
themes.root_cause: Front-line agents cannot see or book specialist diaries and there is no waiting list or callback, so the only option offered is to keep ringing back and hope someone is free.
examples: I have been trying for weeks to get in touch with a tax advisor and was told none are available and that no timeframe can be given.
The customer has been trying for weeks to get in touch with someone about financial counseling services, experiencing transfers, lack of information, and no immediate availability.

themes.name: other: error_not_corrected
themes.problem_statement: Statements about error not corrected that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: the fix an agent promised was never carried out
themes.problem_statement: An agent says the fee, the garnishment, the card or the paperwork will be taken care of, and weeks later nothing has changed and nobody has said why.
themes.root_cause: Promised actions stay as verbal commitments with no ticket, owner or callback, so a back-office step that fails is never noticed until the customer chases it.
examples: A branch banker promised to move the auto loan due date to help avoid late payments and to waive the resulting fees, but the statement shows no change and fees keep being charged.
I was told my previous issue would be resolved and it still has not been addressed.

themes.name: savings interest underpaid for months and never repaid
themes.problem_statement: The interest paid on a savings account or CD is below the agreed rate for months, and even once the fault is acknowledged the shortfall is not paid back.
themes.root_cause: A rate or crediting error in the core system goes undetected until the customer checks the statement, and there is no retroactive adjustment process.
examples: Last month's interest on my savings was lower than usual because of a system glitch, and even after the glitch was fixed the interest still was not corrected.
Interest was not being credited to the savings account because of a system error, and it was only applied once the customer called about it.

themes.name: wrong details on the account file block payments and cards
themes.problem_statement: A wrong routing number, account type, address, phone number or social security number on file stops payments, cards and verification until the customer finds it.
themes.root_cause: Account set-up and change requests are keyed manually with no validation or confirmation back to the customer, so an error sits on the record for months.
examples: The vehicle was repossessed with no option to pay the balance, even though $2,000.00 more than required had already been paid and Chase had the wrong address and phone number on file despite proof of the correct info.
The customer's checking account was recorded in the system as a savings account, something she says she had been trying to tell them, and it was blocking access to her money.

themes.name: paid-off loan still reported late and sent to collections
themes.problem_statement: A payoff, insurance settlement or disputed balance is not applied, so the account keeps showing past due and is reported to credit bureaus or sent to collections.
themes.root_cause: Collections and credit reporting run off the raw balance with no hold placed while a payoff, GAP claim or dispute is still being processed.
examples: The disputed lease-end balance was turned over to a collection agency, dropping an otherwise strong credit score significantly.
A traded-in vehicle's loan was never paid off by the dealership, which later filed bankruptcy, and Chase's continued collection calls and reporting ruined the customer's credit.

themes.name: the error is confirmed but no one is able to reverse it
themes.problem_statement: Staff agree the charge, hold or record is wrong but say it cannot be reversed, adjusted retroactively or changed on their system, so the error simply stands.
themes.root_cause: Front-line teams have no correction rights and post-transaction reversals are barred by policy, leaving a confirmed error with no owner and no route to a fix.
examples: Extra payments of $1000.00 and $200.00 marked for principal only had interest applied instead, and the customer must call after each payment to request the correction.

After following Chase's own instructions to use a Power of Attorney for a lease buyout funded by a personal loan, the title assignment and bill of sale wrongly list the employer as purchaser, and Chase Auto refuses to co

themes.name: the temporary credit is taken back without warning
themes.problem_statement: A provisional or temporary credit for a disputed charge, a failed ATM deposit or a missing payment is paid, spent on essentials, then reversed with no notice, leaving the account overdrawn.
themes.root_cause: Provisional credits are posted before the investigation closes and are clawed back automatically on a negative or merchant-led outcome, with no notice, no explanation and no hardship check.
examples: A grocery purchase that was declined at checkout was still charged to the account, and a temporary credit Chase issued for it was later reversed.
Chase reversed stolen funds back into the joint account, the customer withdrew some to pay a bill, and then Chase reversed the credit again, leaving a deficit.

themes.name: the claim is logged wrong and then denied because of it
themes.problem_statement: The agent logs the wrong charges, the wrong reason or the wrong dates, evidence is never reviewed, and the claim is denied or closed on a deadline the customer was never told about.
themes.root_cause: Claim intake is keyed from the call with no read-back or quality check, and denials are driven by dates and categories rather than by the evidence, with no route to reopen a miskeyed case.
examples: After hundreds of unauthorized charges appeared right after a $5,000.00 deposit, the agent who took her claim disputed the wrong charges and did not dispute all the unauthorized ones.

A $3,500.00 unauthorized payment dispute was denied multiple times for contradictory reasons, including a missed cutoff a supervisor said to ignore and a false claim the customer never disputed the charge.

themes.name: the stop payment or block asked for never took effect
themes.problem_statement: A stop payment, ACH revocation, card cancellation, spending alert or security safeguard is accepted and recorded, but the payment still goes through and the alert never fires.
themes.root_cause: Instructions taken on the call or at the counter are noted on the account but never reach the authorisation and payment systems in time, and nothing checks afterwards that the block actually applied.
examples: Chase confirmed it would not pay a check flagged as fraudulent, but paid it anyway, and the claim filed to recover the funds has exceeded the promised 3-5 business days without resolution.
Despite having a $120.00 spending alert set up, Chase never notified the customer of the fraudulent charges that far exceeded it.

themes.name: closing check mailed to the wrong address or wrong name
themes.problem_statement: The check for the remaining balance is mailed to an old address or made out to a misspelled name, a defunct bank or the wrong person, so the customer cannot cash it and waits weeks for a reissue.
themes.root_cause: Closure payouts are generated from a stale address and name record with no confirmation to the customer before mailing, and each reissue restarts the same manual process.
examples: Checks for the remaining account funds were mailed to the wrong address, and repeated cancellation and reissue requests dragged the process out for weeks.
After closing the inherited account, Chase issued a refund check made out to the name of the defunct predecessor bank, which cannot be cashed anywhere since that bank no longer exists.

themes.name: an old fraud flag still blocks new accounts years later
themes.problem_statement: A fraud marker, 'do not open' flag, deceased marker or reported number from a long-closed or resolved case still blocks new accounts and services, at this bank and at others, for years.
themes.root_cause: Adverse markers are written to internal and industry verification records with no removal step when the case is resolved, and no team owns retracting a report that was wrong.
examples: Chase canceled both business accounts and reported the businesses as fraud to a bank verification service, blocking the customer from opening a new banking relationship elsewhere.
The resulting negative banking history from this incident has caused other financial institutions to turn down the customer's new account applications.

themes.name: rewards points earned on card spending never post
themes.problem_statement: Points, miles or status earned on ordinary card use never post to the account or to the partner programme, and staff can only promise an investigation.
themes.root_cause: Rewards accrual depends on merchant coding and partner feeds that fail silently, with no reconciliation against spend and no front-line right to award the points.
examples: Only 10,000 points showed after months of using the card because the points for an $800 TV purchase never posted; 2,400 points were added manually.
My rewards balance has not changed in a while even though I have been using my card regularly, and it turns out the rewards were not being tracked properly.

themes.name: the sign-up bonus promised at opening is never paid
themes.problem_statement: The bonus, coupon or promotional rate offered when the account was opened is never applied, even after the qualifying spend is met and staff confirm it is owed.
themes.root_cause: The offer is attached by hand at opening and nothing checks it afterwards, so a missed code or a lapsed window leaves no route to pay the bonus retroactively.
examples: A promised direct-deposit bonus was never credited because the branch never gave the required coupon code at account opening, and Chase representatives took no ownership or offered any resolution.
A $750.00 bonus for opening a business checking account with a $20,000.00 deposit and five qualifying debit transactions was never paid, even after a representative confirmed it was owed.

themes.name: a branch deposit is credited short or to another account
themes.problem_statement: Cash, coins or a check handed to a teller are short, credited to someone else's account or debited although the item was handed back, and the difference is never returned.
themes.root_cause: Counter deposits are not counted in front of the customer and no independent recount or audit trail ties the receipt to what was actually posted.
examples: A branch deposit of $2500.00 cash and $150.00 in checks was not counted in front of the customer, and the receipt reflects $1000.00 less than what was actually deposited.
Seven bags of coins deposited at a branch were reported lost, then Chase said the vendor only weighed the bags instead of counting them, so only the declared amount would be credited.

themes.name: a forged or altered check is paid and never refunded
themes.problem_statement: The bank pays a check with a washed amount, a missing payee endorsement or a forged signature, and after admitting it, no money is returned and no safeguard is added.
themes.root_cause: Check acceptance does not test endorsements or alterations against the account's own fraud alerts, and a confirmed forgery has no automatic restitution path.
examples: An earlier counterfeit check attempt was misclassified as a system glitch instead of fraud, so no protective action was taken, allowing two more counterfeit checks totaling $1200.00 to post the next day.
A mortgage check made payable to two parties required both endorsements, but the bank cashed it with only the other payee's signature.

themes.name: the payment left the account but was never credited
themes.problem_statement: A payment sent by check, online or by autopay leaves the customer but is never credited, so the balance stays due, interest runs and the account can be frozen.
themes.root_cause: Payments are matched on keyed account numbers with no validation or exception queue, so a misdirected or held payment sits unposted and nobody reconciles it.
examples: The automatic payment for her credit card bill was not processed although there was enough money in the account, because the system had flagged insufficient funds and held it.
I paid $500 online to my credit card company last Tuesday and it still has not posted a week later, because a typo in the account number sent it to the wrong account.

themes.name: a documented credit dispute is verified as accurate anyway
themes.problem_statement: A documented dispute - identity theft, a late mark on a month paid in full, contradictory data - is answered only with a statement that the reporting is accurate, and the entry stays.
themes.root_cause: Bureau and FCRA disputes are answered by matching the bank's own record rather than reviewing the evidence sent in, and no team is able to retract a report once it has been furnished.
examples: A certified debt validation request citing specific FDCPA and city regulations was answered only with a claim that the reporting is accurate, without any of the required proof documents.
Despite citing the specific federal law requiring it, no notice of dispute was added to the account within the legally required 30-day window.

themes.name: the account is closed without warning and the score drops
themes.problem_statement: Accounts are closed without warning after a hardship request, a dispute or an internal review, and the closure is reported so the score drops, limits are cut and new credit is refused.
themes.root_cause: Risk-driven closures run with no notice, no appeal and no check on whether the account itself was current, and the closure reason is furnished to the bureaus regardless.
examples: The undisclosed account closure was reported to the credit bureaus, and my credit score dropped sharply, leading to reduced credit limits and loan denials.
Enrolling in the hardship program triggered an undisclosed full account review that led to the closure of unrelated accounts that were current and paid on time.

themes.name: points redeemed but the booking or gift card does not work
themes.problem_statement: Points are spent on a booking or a gift card and what arrives is a cheaper room, a flight that was never ticketed or an already-used card, discovered too late to put right.
themes.root_cause: Redemptions are passed to travel and gift-card partners with no confirmation back that the exact item was issued, and the front line cannot reinstate the points or rebook on the spot.
examples: A rewards points redemption for a digital gift card produced an already-used, non-working card, and after reporting it, Chase reissued another already-used card again.
Chase's travel department confirmed a round-trip booking, but the outbound flight was never actually ticketed, making the entire trip unusable hours before departure.

themes.name: reported late despite keeping to the agreed payment plan
themes.problem_statement: The customer keeps to a hardship plan, debt management programme or arrangement an agent set up, and the account is still reported late or charged off.
themes.root_cause: Arrangements live in a servicing note or a separate hardship tool that never reaches collections and credit furnishing, so the account keeps ageing as if no plan existed.
examples: An agent who failed to check the enrollment set up two unauthorized $180.00 payment arrangements and tried to withdraw from a removed account, which effectively and silently ended the debt management plan.
The account was charged off and referred to a collections law firm, which then filed a lawsuit resulting in a default judgment the customer says stems entirely from the company's own errors.

themes.name: the error is corrected and then comes back weeks later
themes.problem_statement: An entry is deleted, reversed or confirmed fixed, and the same delinquency, balance or fraudulent account is back weeks later or still shows on the bank's own screens.
themes.root_cause: Corrections are applied to one report or one system while the source record keeps the original data and re-furnishes it each cycle, and nothing checks that a deletion stayed deleted.
examples: A fraudulent $1400.00 balance was removed from external credit bureau reports but continues to show internally with overdue-payment warning banners.
Two JPMCB credit cards confirmed paid off and closed still generated new delinquencies and late fees, and a subsequent credit report pull showed the same erroneous derogatory information again.

themes.name: the credit inquiry stays after the application is cancelled
themes.problem_statement: An application that was fraudulent, cancelled or caused by the bank's own system failure still leaves hard inquiries on the credit file that nobody will remove.
themes.root_cause: Inquiries are furnished when the application is keyed and there is no retraction step when it is voided, so removal depends on a promise no team owns.
examples: The hard credit inquiry from the approval cannot be reversed even though it resulted entirely from Chase's own system failure.
A fraudulent Chase credit application was canceled with a promise to remove the resulting hard credit inquiries, but nearly a year later they still have not been removed.

themes.name: reported late for a payment the bank itself mishandled
themes.problem_statement: A payment fails, is reversed or arrives late because of the bank's own processing error, and even after the bank admits the fault the delinquency stays on the credit file.
themes.root_cause: Credit furnishing runs off the raw payment record, and there is no retraction step and no owner when the bank's own error, not the customer, caused the missed payment.
examples: Chase issued a card to an unauthorized man on the account, leading to fraudulent charges that were disputed, yet Chase kept reporting late payments and a charge-off from them despite acknowledging its own error.
Despite the payment ultimately going through once corrected, Chase reported the account late and refused to fix it, damaging a previously perfect credit history.

themes.name: the fault is not fixed, only a workaround is offered
themes.problem_statement: A payment service, login or tool is broken and nothing is fixed on the call: the customer is told to retry later, clear cookies, use another method or ring technical support.
themes.root_cause: The technical fault sits with a team the front line cannot reach or raise a ticket with, so agents can only offer scripted workarounds and the customer is left without an owner.
examples: I was offered a digital payment through online banking instead, but that is not what I want; I want Zelle to work.
The only fix offered was clearing cookies and cache, which the customer had already spent a lot of time on alternatives for, and it did not work.

themes.name: escrow fails to pay the property tax or insurance bill
themes.problem_statement: Money is held in escrow but the property tax or insurance premium is paid late, short or not at all, so cover lapses or taxes go delinquent and the penalties land on the customer.
themes.root_cause: Escrow disbursements are made from a stale bill amount with no check that the payment was accepted, so a missed, short or returned payment surfaces only when the tax office or insurer chases.
examples: The escrow statement flagged an issue and the agent found the property tax payment had been missed, which the customer only learned on this call.
An error occurred in the processing of the escrow payment, despite a previous representative stating everything was fine, causing concern about a potential credit score impact.

themes.name: the account stays locked and nobody will unlock it
themes.problem_statement: A security, dormancy or verification lock keeps the customer out of their own account for weeks or months, and the documents sent to lift it are never processed.
themes.root_cause: Locks are set by a back-office risk team the front line cannot reach, with no stated document requirements, no owner and no deadline, so nothing lifts the block.
examples: The asset management account has been locked for weeks due to 'suspicious activity', preventing online login, and no one will clearly state what documentation is required or process the provided documents.
The account was flagged as dormant and weeks of attempts to recover it failed; this agent found the flagging was wrong and escalated to a specialist team that responds within 24 hours.

themes.name: documents already sent in are lost and must be sent again
themes.problem_statement: Documents, applications or requests the customer already submitted cannot be found, and the only fix offered is to start the whole process again from scratch.
themes.root_cause: Submissions enter back-office queues with no tracking reference or acknowledgement to the customer, so an item lost in intake is never traced, only re-requested.
examples: The bank asked for a tax return and proof of income that the customer had already sent with his application; they were misplaced and he has to resubmit them.
The statement requested through the online portal a few days ago was never produced; the agent could not locate it and asked her to re-submit the request through the portal.

themes.name: the app or online banking fault is escalated, never fixed
themes.problem_statement: Online banking, the app, mobile payments or a branch system does not work, every step the agent suggests fails, and the call ends with an escalation instead of a fix.
themes.root_cause: Front-line agents have no diagnostic or fix rights for system faults and can only raise a ticket to a separate technical team, with no timeline and no confirmation back.
examples: The customer was put through to technical support, repeated the whole problem and still left the call without a solution, saying he would report the bank.
I had already restarted the phone and app and re-added the card, then went through the agent's steps again, and it still does not work.

themes.name: no written confirmation the double payment is fixed
themes.problem_statement: A duplicate payment is corrected on the call, but the customer gets nothing in writing showing what changed, so she cannot be sure it will not repeat.
themes.root_cause: The fix to the recurring payment is made verbally with no confirmation letter or case reference, so nothing records what was changed or how a repeat is blocked.
examples: I wanted to know how I can be sure the double payments will not happen again.

themes.name: made to sit through the full briefing after deciding
themes.problem_statement: A customer who has decided to file for bankruptcy is taken through both chapters, the credit effects and every filing step when he only wants the process started.
themes.root_cause: The script mandates a full options-and-consequences briefing before any action, with no short path for a customer who has already chosen.
examples: Had Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 explained, including liquidation versus a three to five year repayment plan, the ten and seven year credit report effects and the debts that cannot be discharged.
Was told the filing steps: gathering income, debt and asset information, preparing the documents and reviewing everything before submitting to the court.

themes.name: another promised email after the first request went nowhere
themes.problem_statement: After an earlier request produced nothing, the remedy is one more emailed link the agent promises to check, so the customer expects to be chasing it again.
themes.root_cause: The failed first request left no tracked case, so the second attempt rests on an agent's personal promise rather than a task the bank follows up.
examples: The agent is emailing me an enrolment link and promised to double-check it, but I have no confidence it will work this time.

themes.name: climate answers with no figures I can check
themes.problem_statement: Asked what the bank actually does on climate, the customer hears branch-level measures, audits and reports, and dismisses them as talk with nothing to verify.
themes.root_cause: Front-line staff have only generic sustainability talking points, with no published figures or named results a customer can check for herself.
examples: Challenged what the bank is actually doing on the environment and climate change, dismissing the branch-level measures as not the big picture.
Doubted the claims were more than talk to appease customers like her and was told third-party auditors verify the practices and a dedicated team reports on progress.

examples: The customer wants to donate to a specific local animal shelter, 'Paws and Claws', which is not on the bank's pre-approved list.
Because I cannot receive post while travelling, the agent arranged a temporary card by courier to my hotel within 24 hours so I can still withdraw cash and pay.

themes.name: my question looked up and answered before the call ended
themes.problem_statement: The customer asks where something is, what a number is or what a process needs, and the agent looks it up and reads it out before the call ends.
themes.root_cause: Branch, ATM and account details sit on the agent's own screen, so the question is answered live instead of being referred on or sent in writing.
examples: Needed to find an ATM close by in San Francisco and was given three nearby addresses on the call.
Asked what is needed to open the account and how to fund it, and was told which documents are required and that the account can be opened within 24 hours.

themes.name: card blocked and claim raised the moment I reported fraud
themes.problem_statement: A fraudulent transaction, a lost card or a forged check is reported, and the agent blocks the card, holds the account and raises the claim before the call ends.
themes.root_cause: Front-line agents can place holds, file the claim and reissue the card themselves, so the exposure stops on the first call rather than waiting for the fraud team.
examples: The bank flagged a suspicious $500 check transaction from last Wednesday that I do not recognise, so I want it reversed and my checks protected.
The customer received a phishing email impersonating Union Financial, requesting login credentials, but did not click the link and reported it to the bank for investigation.

themes.name: the agent did by hand what the app would not do
themes.problem_statement: The online or app route fails - an error, a broken feature, a rejected payment - and the agent carries out the same job manually on the call instead of sending the customer back.
themes.root_cause: Agents can do in their own systems what the digital channel exposes, so a self-service fault does not stop the customer getting the job done.
examples: The customer was unable to download or install the mobile app due to an error, and also had login issues with online banking, which was later identified as an account problem.
The customer was having trouble setting up a charity or fundraising account online for 'Furry Friends Fundraiser'.

themes.name: my payments paused or reduced and applied for on the call
themes.problem_statement: The customer is behind or about to fall behind after losing work, and the agent finds the hardship programme, payment pause or modification that fits and applies for it on the call.
themes.root_cause: Front-line agents can check hardship eligibility and submit the application themselves, so someone in trouble is never left to find the form alone.
examples: Instead of a settlement the agent suggested a hardship program that suspends or reduces payments for a while, and is sending me the application packet.
Unemployed and behind on bills, the customer asked to settle her credit card for about 50% and was offered a hardship programme with suspended payments once she sends her termination letter.

themes.name: my points priced and the trip or gift card booked live
themes.problem_statement: The customer has points but no plan for them, and the agent prices the options against the balance and books the flight, hotel or gift card before the call ends.
themes.root_cause: Agents and the travel desk can see the points balance and complete the redemption live, so the customer never has to work the rewards portal alone.
examples: The agent offered gift cards my points did cover and redeemed a $15 Starbucks card for me with the details to come by email.
A 30,000 point flight, a three-star hotel at 15,000 points a night and a 10,000 point weekend car rental were all booked during the call.

themes.name: an accessible way in arranged around my disability
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot use the phone menus, the app or the branch because of a disability, and the agent arranges an interpreter, a home visit, an accessible branch or another way in.
themes.root_cause: Accessibility services exist - interpreters, home visits, step-free branches, a dedicated line - and front-line agents may arrange them instead of insisting on the standard route.
examples: I called about changing my communication language preference and was asked how I would like to be spoken to, so I asked for slow, clear speech.
The agent found a branch on Elm Street with a flat entrance and no steps and offered directions to it.

themes.name: signed up for the money classes and guides you run
themes.problem_statement: The customer says they do not know where to start with money, and the agent enrols them in a workshop or webinar and sends the guides, videos or tools to work through.
themes.root_cause: A financial education programme exists and agents can register customers for its events and email the material, so nobody is left to find it themselves.
examples: Having inherited her late father's estate she does not know what to do with it, and was booked into the upcoming seminar on wills, trusts and probate.
He wanted to learn about budgeting, saving and investing, and was signed up for the budgeting workshop and an advisor appointment for the savings program.

themes.name: pointed to outside help when it is not a banking matter
themes.problem_statement: What the customer needs is not a banking service at all - tax help, a lawyer, benefits, transport, rent aid - and the agent names the outside body and often applies on their behalf.
themes.root_cause: Agents keep vetted lists of local partners, charities and public programmes and may refer and even complete those applications rather than say it is not our job.
examples: The agent emailed me contact details for partner tax firms and pointed out deductions for charitable contributions, mortgage interest and state and local taxes.
Customer is seeking assistance with transportation to work due to a disability, and the agent provided information for a non-profit.

themes.name: given the contact details of someone outside the bank
themes.problem_statement: What the customer needs is outside what the bank does, and instead of a dead end they are given a named outside organisation or specialist and a working way to reach them.
themes.root_cause: Agents keep and can look up vetted outside contacts - charities, servicers, counsellors, tax and legal specialists - and are allowed to hand them over rather than close the call with a no.
examples: Since the bank could not cover the accessibility costs, I was given the contact details of a non-profit that provides financial assistance for disability adjustments.
The agent offered me contact details for certified tax professionals the bank works with and noted my account for an advisor to reach out.

themes.name: other: clear_communication
themes.problem_statement: Statements about clear communication that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: every fee and rate on my own account stated before I commit
themes.problem_statement: Before the customer commits, the exact fees, rate, minimum balance, limits and penalties on their own account are read out, so no cost appears later as a surprise.
themes.root_cause: Agents have the account's fee schedule and live rate table on screen and read the full cost out, including the conditions that waive it.
examples: I am considering paying my car loan off early and wanted to know the total: $15,000 balance plus a $300 early termination fee comes to $15,600.
After paying off the car loan the customer wanted to be sure there were no early termination fees or other charges left, and was told there are none and that an interest rebate was already credited.

themes.name: walked through the screens until I could do it myself
themes.problem_statement: A customer who cannot find or use a feature in online banking, the mobile app or by text is guided tab by tab until they can complete it themselves.
themes.root_cause: Agents see the same screens as the customer and follow a step-by-step path for each self-service tool instead of only naming where it lives.
examples: I asked how the savings goal tracker works and was shown how to enter the amount, the target date and let the system track my progress.
I also wanted an automatic transfer from checking to savings and was talked through choosing the accounts, the amount and the frequency.

themes.name: bank jargon and notices turned into plain words
themes.problem_statement: Terms such as overdraft protection, APR, APY or endorsement, and letters about a rate or policy change, are explained in everyday language against this account.
themes.root_cause: Agents are trained to translate product jargon and mailed notices, and to check what the change means for the account in front of them.
examples: I learned that co-signing makes me liable for the whole loan and that missed payments would hit my own credit score, which I had not realised.
I asked how interest builds on my $10,000 savings balance and was told it earns 2% APY and is credited monthly, with the year-to-date total visible online.

themes.name: the options compared so I could choose for myself
themes.problem_statement: A customer unsure which account, savings route or arrangement suits them is given each option with its terms and trade-offs, and picks one before the call ends.
themes.root_cause: Agents run a needs-based comparison across the product range, offering the alternative when the first request is not possible, rather than pushing one product.
examples: The agent offered a debt management program that would fold the $10,000 card balance and the $15,000 car loan into one monthly payment with less interest.
The agent offered refinancing or extra principal payments as alternatives, and the customer asked for refinancing information to be sent.

themes.name: the documents, the steps and the timescale given up front
themes.problem_statement: The customer hears exactly which documents, ID and steps are required, what the agent has already done and how long it will take, so the request can move forward.
themes.root_cause: Agents work from a documented checklist per process, check the account live on the call and state the turnaround instead of leaving the customer to wait.
examples: The agent told me about a cosigner release, where after 12 to 24 months of good payments my son could apply to have me removed from the loan.
The customer paid off a $20,000 loan secured on his 2018 Honda Civic and wants the collateral released; documents to sign were to be sent within the hour.

themes.name: the puzzling charge or balance traced and accounted for
themes.problem_statement: An amount the customer does not recognise, a balance that does not match their own records or an item stuck as pending is traced to its source and explained on the call.
themes.root_cause: Agents can see the posting detail behind each item, including when it cleared and who is holding it, so the customer's own record is reconciled live.
examples: The customer's statement balance did not match her own records, and the agent traced it to a $1,000 deposit and small transactions clearing after the statement period.
A transaction had been sitting as pending for a few days; it is a payment to a retailer that the retailer has not processed yet, and the bank cannot speed it up.

themes.name: the fraud alert explained and the account confirmed safe
themes.problem_statement: After a fraud alert, a warning email or a skimming report, the customer is told what triggered it, that the account itself is unaffected, and how to stay safe.
themes.root_cause: Agents can check the flagged activity live and know how the detection rules and phishing patterns work, so they can reassure rather than escalate.
examples: The customer had been getting suspicious activity alerts without understanding them, and learned the fraud system flags unusual transactions as a precaution.
Customer received an email notification about suspicious activity and called to confirm the security status of their account, which was found to be secure.

themes.name: every account, balance and transaction read out on the call
themes.problem_statement: The customer wants the activity itself rather than an explanation, and every account, balance and transaction they need is read out before the call ends.
themes.root_cause: Agents can search across all accounts held under the customer's details and read the history aloud, so no document request or branch visit is needed.
examples: The customer asked for a brief summary of both accounts and was given the deposits, withdrawals and balances: $2,200 on checking and $1,500 on savings.
I wanted all my transactions from the past year across both my checking and savings accounts.

themes.name: what the referral bonus pays and when, before I rely on it
themes.problem_statement: The customer is told exactly what a referral or rewards scheme pays, what triggers each payment and when the credit lands, before they count on the money.
themes.root_cause: Agents have the promotion's qualifying rules and payment timings on screen, so the conditions are stated on the call instead of left in the small print.
examples: The customer learned each successful referral pays $50 into his account and $50 to the person he refers once they open an account.
The agent explained referrals can be made in branch, by referral link or through the website form, and that the credit lands within a few days to a week.

themes.name: a monthly savings figure worked out from my own budget
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot get saving started, so the agent works through their income, bills and goal, names a monthly amount and schedules the transfer on the call.
themes.root_cause: Agents are equipped to do the budget arithmetic live with the customer and turn the resulting figure into a standing transfer before the call ends.
examples: The agent built a monthly budget on the call from a $50,000 salary: $1,500 of fixed costs, $500 a month to the $10,000 card debt and $833 a month towards a $20,000 house deposit.
I want to save for a down payment on a house, so I asked how much I could afford to set aside and had a $500 monthly transfer from checking to savings set up.

themes.name: pointed to the bank's courses when the topic is too big
themes.problem_statement: When the subject is larger than one call - budgeting, saving, tax abroad - the customer is given the bank's courses, articles or webinars to work through afterwards.
themes.root_cause: Agents have a financial education catalogue they can name or email, so a topic too large for a phone answer still leaves the customer something usable.
examples: I wanted to know what resources the bank has on budgeting and saving so I can manage my finances properly.
I wanted to understand the tax implications of keeping a U.S. bank account while living abroad, and it was a lot to take in.

themes.name: the full set of accessibility options listed for me
themes.problem_statement: A customer with a disability hears the whole range at once: Braille statements, Talking and wheelchair-accessible ATMs, the app's screen reader and telephone banking.
themes.root_cause: Accessibility services are not listed anywhere customers look, so the full range only reaches them when an agent reads it out on the call.
examples: I have a physical disability that makes getting around difficult, and I wanted to know what accommodations exist; I was told about Braille statements, wheelchair-accessible ATMs and Talking ATMs.
I asked how to get to my accounts online and was told about the app's screen reader, the keyboard-navigable website and telephone banking.

themes.name: each detail of my own account confirmed through the merger
themes.problem_statement: The customer is told exactly what happens to their own account and routing numbers, login, fees and rewards through the merger, so nothing catches them out later.
themes.root_cause: Merger notices announce the deal without saying what it means for one account, so agents confirm each detail live and email the changed terms.
examples: The customer's checking and savings accounts, account and routing numbers and online banking login all stay the same after the merger, with no change to bill pay or transfers.
The merger simplified the fee structure with some fees eliminated or reduced, and introduced a debit card rewards program, both to be sent by email.

themes.name: the exact branch or ATM, its hours and how to get there
themes.problem_statement: The customer needs somewhere to go and is given the exact branch or ATM, its opening hours, what the machine can do and walking directions before the call ends.
themes.root_cause: Agents have the branch and ATM directory with hours and machine capabilities on screen, so a location question is answered live rather than sent to the website.
examples: The customer asked for ATMs near zip code 94107 and got three locations with hours and deposit capability, the closest one identified and walking directions to it.
I asked what time my local branch opens and was told the Main Street branch opens at 9am Monday to Friday.

themes.name: shown how to stop the fee happening again, and set up
themes.problem_statement: After a charge or a fee change, the customer is given concrete ways to avoid it next time - a waiver, overdraft cover, an alert or a cheaper plan - and it is set up on the call.
themes.root_cause: Agents can see which waivers, linked accounts, alerts and plans apply to this account, so they close the call with a prevention step, not just the fee.
examples: The agent also mentioned the updated mobile app, where I can check balances and transaction history and set balance alerts.
I asked how to avoid these fees and was told to withdraw cash at an ATM, look at an account designed for international travel, or use a card without foreign transaction fees.

themes.name: a parent shown how to watch and cap a child's spending
themes.problem_statement: A parent who cannot see or limit what a child spends is given the full set of controls - visibility, alerts, spending limits, blocked merchants - and where to switch them on.
themes.root_cause: Youth account monitoring and restriction settings are buried in online banking, so parents only get the full set when an agent lists them and sets them up.
examples: I wanted to manage my child's spending; a joint account gives me full visibility and category controls let me block things like video game stores or streaming services.
The customer wanted to limit what his newly 13-year-old son can spend and reach, and the agent explained the Youth Account Restrictions in online banking and how to set them up.

themes.name: told which green options I can actually have, and enrolled
themes.problem_statement: A customer who wants greener banking is told what the bank actually does, which green products they can have where they live, and is signed up for paperless on the call.
themes.root_cause: Green initiatives and products are announced without saying who is eligible, so agents name the concrete measures, check availability and enrol the customer.
examples: Wants to know the bank is doing its part on the environment and is told about LED lighting in branches, paperless statements and online banking.
Green checking, solar loans and a recycled-material credit card were described, but only the green checking account can be opened here as the others are limited to select locations.

themes.name: how to build a first credit history from nothing
themes.problem_statement: A customer with no card or loan of their own, wanting a car or a house later, is given the concrete first steps into credit and how long each takes to show.
themes.root_cause: The route into a first credit history - secured card, authorised user, small loan, on-time payments, utilisation under 30% - is published nowhere, so only an agent sets it out.
examples: I am a recent graduate with only a student loan and a part-time job, and I want to build a credit score good enough for a car loan and eventually a mortgage.
I am a first-time buyer who has never had a loan or a credit card, and I want to know how to build a credit history for a car or a house later.

themes.name: how to place a fraud alert or credit freeze after a leak
themes.problem_statement: A customer whose details may be exposed needs to know how to protect them: monitor accounts, place a fraud alert or a freeze with the three bureaus, and the warning signs to watch for.
themes.root_cause: Identity protection sits with the three credit bureaus and the FTC rather than the bank, so the alert, freeze and monitoring steps only reach the customer when an agent walks through them.
examples: I asked how to stop identity theft happening again and was told how to protect my information, monitor my reports and what to do if someone already has my details.
I was told a fraud alert would make creditors verify my identity, and that I can place one by contacting any of the three credit reporting agencies.

themes.name: why my credit score moved and what would raise it
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot see why their score is what it is, or why it dropped despite on-time payments, and needs the factors behind it plus concrete steps and a realistic timeframe to raise it.
themes.root_cause: A score is published as a number with no breakdown, so the weight of payment history, utilisation, credit age and new inquiries is only explained when an agent spells it out.
examples: My credit score dropped even though I have made every payment on time, and I wanted to know why.
I wanted practical steps to raise my score, and was told to keep my utilisation ratio low and keep paying on time.

themes.name: getting my credit report and disputing a wrong entry
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot get hold of their credit report or make sense of an entry on it, and needs to know how to pull the free reports, read each line and dispute what is wrong.
themes.root_cause: The free annual reports and the dispute route sit with the three bureaus and their entry wording is opaque, so agents have to walk the customer through both.
examples: I wanted to see my credit report to find out what is going on, and signed up for the free credit monitoring service.
I asked what to do if I find something wrong on my credit report.

themes.name: which hardship or relief programme I qualify for
themes.problem_statement: A customer who has lost income or fallen behind does not know which relief programmes exist, what each one does to the payments or whether they qualify, and is left to guess.
themes.root_cause: Forbearance, modification and external assistance schemes are documented only in an internal hardship playbook, so eligibility is checked against the account only when an agent looks.
examples: HARP and HAMP were explained as routes to lower payments, with the advice to speak to a housing counsellor about eligibility.
I was walked through forbearance to suspend or reduce payments temporarily, and loan modification options such as a lower interest rate or a longer repayment term.

themes.name: how my money is protected and what I can do myself
themes.problem_statement: With nothing wrong on the account, a customer worried about fraud is told what the bank's own safeguards are and which precautions to take, rather than being reassured in general terms.
themes.root_cause: The bank's security measures and the precautions a customer can take are not set out anywhere they look, so agents work through a security checklist and set the protections up on the call.
examples: I have not noticed anything unusual on my accounts, but identity theft is becoming more common and I want to know what steps I can take to keep my personal information secure.
The agent walked the customer through changing her password, enabling two-factor authentication and monitoring her transaction history for anything suspicious.

themes.name: what the bank actually does for the community
themes.problem_statement: A customer asking what the bank does for the community or the environment gets concrete programmes, examples and ways to take part instead of a general statement of good intentions.
themes.root_cause: Community, environmental and lending-commitment work only appears in reports and mailed letters, so agents keep a list of concrete examples to read out when asked.
examples: I wanted to be sure my bank is doing good things for the community, and I had no idea about the volunteering programme and the financial education workshops.
I asked what the bank is actually doing on the environment after the letter, and how suppliers are held to the same standards.

themes.name: the bank's own security measures described
themes.problem_statement: A customer worried about fraud, hacking or data loss asks what actually protects their accounts, data or deposits, and hears the specific safeguards in place.
themes.root_cause: The bank's security controls are not published anywhere customers read, so encryption, monitoring, access rules and physical measures only reach them when an agent lists them.
examples: The customer asked what protects her employees' sensitive information and was told about encryption, secure servers, access controls and regular audits.
I asked whether my personal information is still accessible on the stolen phone and what happens if someone tries to reach my accounts another way.

themes.name: practical steps to keep my own accounts safe
themes.problem_statement: A customer who has lost nothing asks how to avoid phishing, skimming or identity theft, and is given concrete habits and settings to use rather than a general reassurance.
themes.root_cause: Agents have fraud-prevention guidance to hand and walk through passwords, two-factor authentication, alerts and credit monitoring instead of waiting for a loss to happen.
examples: The customer requested steps and tips to protect themselves from future ATM skimming scams.
The customer asked for general advice and was told about strong unique passwords, phishing, checking for https, keeping software updated and avoiding public Wi-Fi.

themes.name: the bank's community and green programmes spelled out
themes.problem_statement: A customer asking what the bank does for the community or the environment is told the actual programmes, what each funds or matches, and how to take part.
themes.root_cause: Community, charity-matching and environmental commitments are published only as headlines, so the named programmes, limits and sign-up routes reach the customer only on the call.
examples: The customer works for a non-profit looking for a bank with a charity matching programme and wanted the approved charity list and the maximum match per donation.
A letter told me about the bank's community programs but not which ones run in my area, so I asked where to find that.

themes.name: the scholarships laid out with amounts and deadlines
themes.problem_statement: A customer asking about the bank's scholarships hears which programmes exist, what each awards, who qualifies, the documents needed and the closing date.
themes.root_cause: Scholarship programmes sit scattered across the website, so agents read the award amounts, eligibility rules, application pack and deadlines out in a single call.
examples: As a college student paying tuition I asked what scholarships the bank offers and was told about the Scholars, Community and STEM programs worth $500 to $2,000 a year.
I asked how to apply and what the selection criteria are, and was told about the transcript, recommendation letter, personal statement and the early spring deadline.

themes.name: which team or outside body handles it, and its number
themes.problem_statement: A request the general line cannot settle leaves the customer needing the right team's or outside body's name, direct number and email instead of having to find them alone.
themes.root_cause: Specialist teams and outside bodies are listed only in an internal directory, so a handover is made explicit with contact details only when an agent reads it out.
examples: The agent gave me the legal department's direct phone number and email so I can get the power of attorney started.
The agent gave me the Estate Services department's phone number and email so I can carry on with the estate there.

themes.name: the nearest branch, its hours and how to get there
themes.problem_statement: A customer who wants to come in is given the branch closest to them, its opening hours and directions before the call ends, instead of hunting on the website.
themes.root_cause: Agents can search the branch network by location with hours and mapping to hand, so the nearest branch and the way to it are given on the call.
examples: I asked about your branch locations and hours and then which branch is closest to my zip code and how to get to it.
The customer asked for assistance in finding the nearest branch and received clear directions to a branch on Main Street in downtown LA.

themes.name: the return window, fees and rights on what I bought
themes.problem_statement: A customer unhappy with a purchase made through the bank or an affiliate does not know the return and exchange window, the fees that apply, or what they can insist on from the merchant.
themes.root_cause: Merchant terms behind a purchase are visible to agents but not to the customer, so the refund window, restocking fees and consumer rights are only stated on the call.
examples: Customer wants to understand the options for exchanging a recently purchased laptop, including policy details and potential fees.
An $800 laptop bought on January 15th arrived without a charger and the merchant refused to supply one; the agent explained her rights and the routes open to her.

themes.name: what protects my account, and the safeguards switched on
themes.problem_statement: A customer worried about hacking, a breach or a fake email is told what actually guards the account and has two-factor login, biometrics or alerts switched on during the call.
themes.root_cause: Two-factor login, biometrics and custom alerts are off by default and hard to find, so customers only learn they exist and get them enabled when an agent walks them through it.
examples: After inheriting a large sum, the customer asked how the account could be protected; the agent covered two-factor authentication, biometric login and 24/7 fraud monitoring.
The agent provided clear steps to secure the customer's Facebook account, including changing passwords and enabling two-factor authentication, and sent a helpful link for online safety.

themes.name: which scholarship or grant I can apply for, and its rules
themes.problem_statement: Someone asking about the bank's scholarships, grants or awards cannot find each programme's amount, eligibility rules, deadline or where to apply, and needs them read out.
themes.root_cause: Award criteria sit under a community tab customers cannot find, so amounts, GPA rules and deadlines only reach an applicant when an agent reads the programme sheet.
examples: I asked what educational scholarships and grants the bank offers and was given the three programmes, their amounts, GPA requirements and deadlines.
The grant program gives $5,000 to $20,000 for equipment, hiring or renovation, and applications go through the website or a branch where business development officers help.

themes.name: today's exchange rate and how to avoid conversion fees
themes.problem_statement: A customer travelling or sending money abroad needs today's rates, a frank word on where they may move, and the practical ways to keep the conversion charges down.
themes.root_cause: Rates move daily and conversion fees are buried in card terms, so the live rate and the fee-avoiding routes are only read out on the call.
examples: I asked what the exchange rates are now and whether they are likely to move, and was given the Euro, Pound and Yen rates with the factors behind them.
I decided to exchange on arrival, and the agent added advice about shopping around for fees and carrying some local currency for immediate expenses.

themes.name: the hardship help I qualify for, named and explained
themes.problem_statement: A customer out of work, ill or otherwise struggling is told which relief schemes or concessionary products they may qualify for, what they must show and where to apply.
themes.root_cause: Government and hardship schemes sit outside the product catalogue, so only an agent keeping the eligibility rules to hand can point a struggling customer at one.
examples: I have been out of work for several months and am struggling to make ends meet, so I wanted to know which government relief programmes I might qualify for.
Out of work for months and struggling, the customer asked what relief programmes exist and was told about the loan programmes and CARES Act support and where to apply.

themes.name: branch hours, address and nearest ATM, and what to bring
themes.problem_statement: A customer who has to go in - for a notary, a safe deposit box, a deposit - needs the nearest branch, its address and hours, what to bring, and where the nearest ATM is.
themes.root_cause: Branch and ATM hours, locations and in-branch services are incomplete or out of date online, so agents read them from the internal directory instead.
examples: The agent found three network ATMs in San Francisco and gave the customer the addresses and turn-by-turn directions to the nearest one.
Asked for branch hours and the addresses of the three branches open on Saturdays and was given both on the call.

themes.name: what protects my money, and what I should do myself
themes.problem_statement: A customer worried about fraud does not know what the bank does to keep the account safe or what they should do themselves, and needs the protections plus a practical checklist.
themes.root_cause: The bank's security measures and fraud prevention advice are not set out anywhere customers look, so the whole picture only reaches them when an agent reads it out.
examples: Asked what protects the account and was told about encryption, two-factor authentication, trusted device registration and a dedicated fraud detection team.
I asked how the bank protects my business's money in the lockbox and was told about steel boxes, anti-theft devices, bonded couriers and regular audits.

themes.name: what the bank does in the community and how to join in
themes.problem_statement: A customer asking about the bank's community, CRA and charitable work hears the actual programmes, recent projects and the ways to partner, volunteer or apply.
themes.root_cause: Community investment work is reported to regulators rather than to customers, so agents have to describe the programmes and name the owning team on the call.
examples: The agent did give a general description of the affordable housing, small business and community facility loans and the revitalisation projects the bank invests in.
I am looking for community programmes for my two children under 10 so they have some positive influences in their lives.

themes.name: pointed to the help that sits outside the bank
themes.problem_statement: When the answer lies outside the bank, the customer is told which government relief or benefits programme, outside professional or complaints body applies and where to go.
themes.root_cause: Agents keep a referral list of external programmes and professionals with their eligibility rules, so a customer the bank cannot help directly still leaves with a route.
examples: The laptop's battery life and screen resolution are worse than the customer was led to believe, and she did not know whether to return it or have it repaired.
The customer asked how long she has to decide and whether repair is possible, and was told 30 days typically applies subject to the seller's policy.

themes.name: what my gift card can buy and when it expires
themes.problem_statement: A card the customer was given rather than bought comes with no terms, so they do not know where it works online or in store, what it cannot buy, or when it expires.
themes.root_cause: Gift and prepaid cards arrive with no terms attached, so acceptance rules, excluded transactions and the expiry date only reach the holder when an agent reads the conditions out.
examples: The customer did not know whether a gift card received from a friend could be used online or only in-store, and was told it works both ways.
I received a gift card as a present and did not know whether there were restrictions on its use or specific merchants where I could use it.

themes.name: other: fair_outcome
themes.problem_statement: Statements about fair outcome that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: the bank's own error was found and refunded on the call
themes.problem_statement: The customer is charged a fee or finds a wrong balance, statement or account setting; the agent checks, confirms the bank's own error and credits the money back during the same call.
themes.root_cause: Front-line agents can see the posting history behind the charge and have authority to reverse the bank's own error themselves instead of routing it to a back-office review.
examples: I was charged an overdraft fee on a $20 purchase last week when I thought my account had enough in it, and I had no notification about a low balance.
I received a letter from you with my account information printed on it and worried someone could have intercepted it; it turned out the letter was sent in error.

themes.name: money taken without authorisation was credited back
themes.problem_statement: Money taken by an unauthorised or fraudulent transaction, or sent to the wrong payee, is reversed or provisionally credited while the dispute runs, so the customer is not left out of pocket.
themes.root_cause: Agents can raise the dispute and release a provisional credit on the call under the fraud policy, instead of making the customer wait for the investigation to finish.
examples: A $500 payment to John Smith was made in error; the agent located it and processed a refund back to the debit card within 3-5 business days.
An unauthorized $500 purchase was made on January 1st with an unrecognized merchant; the transaction was reversed by the agent.

themes.name: a valid fee was waived as a goodwill gesture
themes.problem_statement: The charge is valid and no bank error is found, but the agent waives the fee or applies a courtesy credit for a first slip or for the trouble caused, often without being asked.
themes.root_cause: Agents hold a one-time courtesy allowance they can apply at their own discretion, so an honest mistake or a wasted second call does not have to be escalated.
examples: A $10 overdraft fee was charged because a store purchase took me $1 over, and the agent reversed it once she saw it was accidental.
The agent set up overdraft protection so future shortfalls are covered from a linked account, waived the $30 fee as a one-time courtesy and suggested balance alerts.

themes.name: moved onto the better deal the customer qualified for
themes.problem_statement: The customer sits on a product or rate worse than their balance, status or a running promotion entitles them to; the agent spots it and switches them over on the call.
themes.root_cause: Agents review eligibility, loyalty benefits and live promotions against the account in front of them and can open or switch the product during the same call.
examples: The customer was offered a choice of referral benefits and picked the cash deposit into her checking account, which the agent applied with funds due within 24 hours.
On the strength of a steady $10,000 balance with no withdrawals for a year, the agent moved the customer to the Platinum Savings Account at 1.75% APY.

themes.name: a workable alternative offered when the answer was no
themes.problem_statement: The bank cannot do what is asked - waive the fee, expedite the card, skip the penalty, take the payment now - and the agent offers an alternative that solves it rather than stopping at no.
themes.root_cause: Agents have hardship, deferment and substitute-product options at hand and are expected to offer them when policy blocks the customer's original request.
examples: The agent checked my eligibility and enrolled me in the financial hardship programme, which suspends my payments while a catch-up plan is worked out.
After unexpected medical bills the customer missed a car loan payment; the agent granted a one-time deferment moving the due date two weeks out with no late fees or penalties.

themes.name: the routine request was completed on the call
themes.problem_statement: A routine request - open or change an account, set up a report, order a replacement, send a statement - is carried out by the agent before the call ends.
themes.root_cause: Agents can complete routine account admin end to end from the phone, so the customer needs no form, no branch visit and no second contact.
examples: Customer requested research on historical account activity to track down suspicious charges from a few months ago and ensure no unauthorized transactions remain.
The customer needs to replace worn-out coins and the bank offers a courier service to pick them up.

themes.name: Fraud stopped on the call before more money left
themes.problem_statement: A forged check, a lost card or suspicious activity is caught, and the agent puts a stop payment, a card block or an account hold on at once so no more money leaves.
themes.root_cause: Agents can place stop payments, card blocks and account holds themselves as soon as fraud is suspected, ahead of the fraud department's investigation.
examples: The verification department took the account and check number and stopped payment on the check.
I lost my debit card getting off a train in Europe and only noticed days later; the card was eventually stopped and a replacement ordered for 7-10 business days.

themes.name: Part of the overdue balance written off to settle it
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot clear a balance they have fallen behind on; the bank accepts a lump sum for less than the full amount and treats the rest as paid in full.
themes.root_cause: Collections agents hold delegated settlement authority and can agree a discounted lump sum, with fees and interest written off, without a separate recovery review.
examples: After losing her job the customer could not keep up with a $10,000 credit card balance, and was offered a settlement of $6,000 with the remaining $4,000 treated as paid in full.
I owe $5,000 on my credit card and asked about settling it; the offer started at $3,500 and the agent came back with $3,200 as a one-time payment.

themes.name: Wrong credit-file mark removed or disputed for me
themes.problem_statement: A late payment or an unknown debt is reported on the customer's credit file although it is wrong; the entry is removed or the bureau dispute is raised for them on the call.
themes.root_cause: Agents can see the true posting history and are authorised to correct bureau reporting or raise the dispute on the customer's behalf instead of sending them to the bureau.
examples: The credit report showed a missed payment although the customer paid that bill on time; the agent checked the payment history and removed the entry.
The bank is disputing both entries with the credit bureau, to be corrected within a few days with nothing more for me to do.

themes.name: Several debts consolidated into one cheaper payment
themes.problem_statement: The customer is juggling loans and card balances at different rates, and the agent prices one consolidation loan that cuts the monthly payment and the interest paid.
themes.root_cause: Agents can run the consolidation arithmetic against the customer's own debts and originate the replacement loan on the call, so the saving is agreed before it ends.
examples: A $15,000 car loan at 6%, an $8,000 personal loan at 8% and a $3,000 credit card at 12% were consolidated into one loan at 5% with a $450 monthly payment, saving around $1,200 in interest.
Consolidating the high-interest student loan and credit card debt into one lower-rate loan would save around $300 per month and leave a single payment.

themes.name: Emergency cash approved and paid in the same day
themes.problem_statement: The customer needs cash now for a car repair, a medical bill or rent, and a capped advance or emergency loan is approved on the call and paid in within the hour.
themes.root_cause: Agents can approve a small emergency advance against the account without a full application, so the money arrives while the customer is still on the phone.
examples: Customer was in a difficult financial situation needing emergency cash and successfully prequalified for a personal loan of up to $5,000 after overdraft protection was insufficient.
She has an unexpected medical bill she cannot cover after losing her job, did not want overdraft protection and needed the money immediately.

themes.name: Account fees on the statement nobody flagged at opening
themes.problem_statement: Monthly maintenance, inactivity, out-of-network ATM or service fees appear on the statement of an account the customer believed was free.
themes.root_cause: Fee conditions such as a minimum balance or an account tier are set at opening and nothing warns the customer in the month the condition is missed.
examples: I saw a $20 maintenance fee on my statement and did not know why; it was charged because my balance fell below $1,500 for a period.
There is a $10 fee and a $5 fee on my statement and I did not know what they were or why I was charged twice.

themes.name: Overdraft fee on a payment the customer thought was covered
themes.problem_statement: A card purchase, check or recurring payment goes through against an insufficient balance and an overdraft or overdraft protection fee is charged before the customer sees it coming.
themes.root_cause: The available balance shown to the customer does not reflect pending or scheduled items, and no low balance alert is sent before the transaction posts.
examples: A $20 charge on the youth account turned out to be an overdraft fee from a store purchase the customer did not realise had overdrawn her account, and it cannot be waived.
I saw a $35 overdraft fee charged yesterday when I checked my account online, and I thought I had enough money in my account.

themes.name: A charge on the statement the customer never made
themes.problem_statement: An unrecognised, duplicate or unauthorised charge appears on the account and the customer has to raise a dispute to find out where it came from.
themes.root_cause: Merchant duplicates, card compromise and posting errors reach the account unchecked, so the customer is the first line of detection rather than the bank.
examples: A payment to a store appeared on the statement that the customer says she did not make; it turned out to be a duplicate charge and was reversed on the call.
A $50 charge from Joe's Diner on January 1st appeared on the debit card for a restaurant the customer did not eat at, and the dispute was opened for investigation.

themes.name: A one-off fee attached to the action just taken
themes.problem_statement: A specific action - using the card abroad, buying a cashier's check, breaking a term early, amending or paying late - carries its own fee or penalty the customer had not counted on.
themes.root_cause: Per-transaction fees and penalties sit in the product's fee schedule and are not put in front of the customer at the moment they commit to the action.
examples: Taking any of the principal out before maturity costs 90 days' interest on the amount withdrawn, and the same applies if I take the whole balance.
There may be fees for making changes to my term deposit and they were not waived.

themes.name: Rate or price charged higher than the amount expected
themes.problem_statement: The interest rate, finance charge, late fee, quoted price or escrow payment is higher than the customer expected or believes is allowed, so the size of the amount is the issue.
themes.root_cause: Rate moves, statutory caps and escrow or pricing recalculations are applied without an explanation the customer can check against what they were originally told.
examples: Late fees ranging from $25.00 to $37.00 were charged repeatedly, which the customer believes exceed the CFPB's $8.00 safe harbor threshold for large credit card issuers.
The same flight for the same passengers and date became available for $600.00 per ticket less shortly after the original Chase booking, making the original a duplicate at an inflated price.

themes.name: the only team that can help is unavailable when called
themes.problem_statement: The customer holds, is transferred again or is promised a callback because the department or specialist that owns their request is busy, booked out or not taking calls.
themes.root_cause: Requests are handled only by one back-office team or named specialist, with no cover and no queued callback, so the customer waits on that team's availability.
examples: The account opening department was busy, so I was asked to hold twice before anyone could take over the application.
The last time I called in I had to wait on hold for a while, though the representative who took the call was helpful and fixed the issue quickly.

themes.name: no one can say how long the wait or decision will take
themes.problem_statement: Asked how long a hold, an outage or a decision will take, the agent has no figure to give, so the customer waits without knowing whether it means minutes or weeks.
themes.root_cause: Queue wait times, incident ETAs and case timelines are not surfaced to front-line agents, who can only say that it depends on call volume.
examples: I was transferred to the billing department and could not be told how long the wait would be.
The application submitted a few days ago is still being processed and no exact timeline for a decision could be given; nothing further is needed from the customer for now.

themes.name: identity questions I cannot answer stall the call
themes.problem_statement: The customer answers question after question about employers, schools or old addresses, is put back on hold, and still cannot be verified before anything can be done.
themes.root_cause: Verification leans on stale credit-file questions that do not fit every customer's life, with no fallback check when the answers do not match.
examples: Was taken through date of birth, address, her last branch visit and whether she had spoken to a representative before being told the question needed another team.
Was held on the line through question after question, including her employer, high school and college, none of which applied to a stay-at-home mother with a GED and no college.

themes.name: nothing told me my request was backlogged or waiting on me
themes.problem_statement: An application, a closure or a set of documents sits for days with no update, and only when the customer calls do they learn it is backlogged or waiting on something from them.
themes.root_cause: Nothing updates the customer or asks for the missing document while a case waits in a queue, so progress depends on the customer calling in to chase it.
examples: I applied for a credit card a few days ago and have heard nothing; it turns out there is a backlog and a decision is still a few business days away.
The customer heard nothing for days about his credit card application and learned on the call that it is on hold until he sends proof of income, employment and address.

themes.name: a fixed turnaround of days with no way to speed it up
themes.problem_statement: The letter, card, deposit, transfer, report or review carries a fixed lead time of days or weeks that cannot be shortened, and the customer needs it sooner than that.
themes.root_cause: These steps run on batch processing or on postal and third-party timescales, and no expedited route is offered when the customer's own deadline is tighter.
examples: The notarized lien release letter will take 7-10 business days to arrive before the customer can go to the DMV.
The application takes about two weeks to process, which is a long time for us, so the agent offered a temporary debit card to reach the funds in the meantime.

themes.problem_statement: Statements about incorrect or conflicting information that fit no specific theme.
