themes.name: conflicting answers given for the same figure or date
themes.problem_statement: The customer is given one figure, date or explanation and then a different one for the same item, with no correction.
themes.root_cause: Agents quote from memory or from different records and nothing checks a second answer against the first before the call ends.
examples: The interest on the statement was given first as $525.00 and then as $125.00 in the same conversation.
The tiers I was given overlap: 1.5% for a balance of $0 to $5000, 2% for $501 to $1,000 and 2.5% for over $1,000.

themes.name: service offered, then withdrawn and handed to another team
themes.problem_statement: An agent starts the request or describes a service, then withdraws it and sends the customer to a different number or department.
themes.root_cause: Front-line scripts and product lists are out of step with what each team is actually allowed to handle.
examples: She was told a new debit card with the updated address had been ordered for 7-10 business days, then told the request had to be transferred to Card Services after all.
The agent quoted a $20 monthly fee waived at a $5,000 average balance but admitted the fee schedule had changed, and transferred me to a colleague with current figures.

themes.name: wrong or missing account details block verification
themes.problem_statement: Identity checks and account lookups fail, or the wrong account is found, because the data on file is wrong, missing or mislabelled.
themes.root_cause: Keying errors and gaps at onboarding and after life events leave account records that no longer match the customer.
examples: The employer rejected the routing number the customer gave for direct deposit; the bank found an error in its own system and issued the correct routing number to use instead.
I was verified at the start of the call but then asked again for my social security number because it was not on file.

themes.name: notice states a balance or debt the account does not show
themes.problem_statement: A letter, bill, statement or credit report entry states something the account itself does not show, such as a balance, a due date or a debt.
themes.root_cause: Notices and reported figures are built from stale or mis-keyed data and are never reconciled with the live account before being sent.
examples: I received a letter saying my account balance exceeded the insured amount, and it turned out to be a system error that had already been corrected.
Customer received a letter stating their account was compromised due to potential fraudulent activity, but the agent could not provide specific details about the activity.

themes.name: promotion described in marketing is not actually offered
themes.problem_statement: A promotion, flyer, website page or earlier tip leads the customer to expect a rate, event or programme the bank does not actually offer.
themes.root_cause: Marketing, branch material and third-party channels are not kept in step with current product terms and event calendars.
examples: Her friend mentioned a discount on the loan interest rate, but it was not in the promotion details and only applies to certain loan products.
The customer had heard the referral program also discounted his own account fees, and was told the current program does not offer that.

themes.name: other: denied_or_declined_without_explanation
themes.problem_statement: Statements about denied or declined without explanation that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: nothing I give matches, so I am sent somewhere else
themes.problem_statement: Every identifier the customer gives fails to match, so the request is refused, escalated or sent to another channel with no reason given for the mismatch.
themes.root_cause: Records are out of date or mis-keyed and agents have no fallback route once the standard verification questions fail.
examples: Wanted to enroll in text banking but could not be verified on the phone, so she was told to visit a branch to be identified in person.
When I called back about my account, nothing I gave would locate it and I was told to call the customer service line instead.

themes.name: declined on a score, with nothing I can act on next time
themes.problem_statement: A loan, settlement or eligibility request is turned down citing a score or criteria, without the detail the customer would need to qualify next time.
themes.root_cause: Decisioning sits in systems the front line cannot see into, so agents can repeat the outcome but not explain the deciding factors.
examples: The customer asked to settle her credit card debt for less than the full amount, but did not qualify for the debt settlement program and was offered a credit counselor instead.
I applied for a loan recently and was denied, and I want to improve my chances of being approved next time.

themes.name: the waiver, due-date move or rate I asked for is not offered
themes.problem_statement: The change or relief asked for - a fee waiver, a due-date move, a better rate, a replacement - is ruled out by policy or by the system itself.
themes.root_cause: Product rules are hard-coded with no exception path, so agents can only state the refusal and offer an unrelated alternative.
examples: I was told the fees cannot be waived because they are generated automatically, and was transferred to the customer loyalty department instead.
I am hoping to get a better interest rate on my existing term deposit.

themes.name: I only learn of the block when a payment fails
themes.problem_statement: An account, card or payment is suspended, stopped or closed by a risk decision the customer only discovers when something fails at the checkout or online.
themes.root_cause: Fraud and closure decisions are taken automatically and the reason is withheld from both the customer and the agent on the call.
examples: I was never told why my account was suspended and I have not done anything out of the ordinary as far as I know.
The card was declined at checkout buying a laptop because a hold had been placed on the account for suspicious activity.

themes.name: the referral bonus was never paid after approval
themes.problem_statement: A referred application was approved but the bonus promised for it never appeared on the referring customer's account.
themes.root_cause: Referral tracking does not reliably link an approved application back to the referring account, so the reward never posts.
examples: After a cousin's card application through the customer's referral link was approved, the promised referral bonus points were never credited.

themes.name: other: system_or_app_failure
themes.problem_statement: Statements about system or app failure that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Login blocked by a wrong-credential or unknown-device error
themes.problem_statement: Login returns invalid username or password, or an unrecognised device, and password resets and browser changes do not restore access.
themes.root_cause: Authentication or the account's online profile is broken, and the front line can only suggest generic browser fixes or hand the case on.
examples: I also keep getting an error message when logging in to online banking, which could not be looked at without sharing my username and password.
I am also having trouble logging in to my online banking account, which had to be passed to the IT department.

themes.name: Agent's system cannot pull up my account on the call
themes.problem_statement: Correct account numbers and identifiers do not pull up the record, or a system error blocks the agent, so the request cannot be handled.
themes.root_cause: Lookup and record systems fail to index accounts, especially after a move or a name change, leaving agents with no working search.
examples: The agent could not find my account from the account number I double-checked, and asked for my social security number, which I did not want to give by phone.
I could not activate my debit card because the system is still processing the address change from my move last weekend.

themes.name: Card errors at the pump, the ATM and the phone wallet
themes.problem_statement: The card is declined or returns a reader error at pumps, ATMs and digital wallets with funds available, or still works after it expired.
themes.root_cause: Terminal and authorisation faults on the bank or merchant side go undetected, so the card behaves differently from what the systems say.
examples: Adding my card to Apple Pay keeps returning Card Not Supported, and deleting and re-adding the card did not help.
My debit card kept giving a card error at the gas pump even after trying a different pump, although there is plenty of money in my account.

themes.name: Online or in-app task errors out and forces a call
themes.problem_statement: An online or in-app action - a payment, an enrolment, a form, a download, an install - fails with an error, forcing a call or a manual fix.
themes.root_cause: Web and app journeys break on particular accounts, browsers and devices and there is no working fallback inside the channel itself.
examples: Tried to move the account to another branch through online banking but it would not go through, so he had to call.
The online reorder checks page shows no check options and says none are available for reorder even though I know I have plenty left; it was fixed on the call.

themes.name: Payment taken twice, missed or pushed to another month
themes.problem_statement: A payment is taken twice, never processed although it showed as successful, or pushed to another month by a processing system issue.
themes.root_cause: Payment processing retries and reschedules without reconciling against what has already been posted to the account.
examples: A $500 payment made on Wednesday was never processed because of a technical glitch at the bank, although online banking showed the payment as successful.
A payment I made to a vendor shows up twice on my statement with different dates, and the agent could not verify the error on their side.

themes.name: merger changes the account but details come later
themes.problem_statement: The merger changes account numbers, cards, ATMs, fees and rates, and the customer is told the specifics will follow in a later letter.
themes.root_cause: Product alignment decisions are still open while customers are already being notified, so the front line has no final answer to give.
examples: The fee structure is being streamlined so some fees rise and some fall, and some interest rates change; a detailed statement is promised before anything takes effect.
The checking monthly maintenance fee goes from $8 to $10, the overdraft fee falls from $35 to $25, and the savings annual fee changes as part of the merger.

themes.name: fee or overdraft change notice does not say what it costs me
themes.problem_statement: A maintenance, overdraft, ATM or wire fee rises, or overdraft cover changes, and the notice does not say what it means for this account.
themes.root_cause: Fee change notices state the new schedule but are not tailored to the account, so customers call to work out their own position.
examples: I had heard something about changes to overdraft fees; the new service moves money from savings to checking to avoid them, and I had to opt in, which the agent did on the call.
The policy update email changed the overdraft fees, and the customer wanted to know whether those changes would affect his account.

themes.name: rate change notice gives no figure for my own balance
themes.problem_statement: A letter or statement announces a savings, mortgage, loan or card rate change and the customer cannot tell what it does to what they earn or pay.
themes.root_cause: Rate change notices give the percentage and the date but no worked figure for the customer's own balance or monthly payment.
examples: The savings account rate fell from 3% to 2.5% in the recent rate change, so the customer will earn slightly less interest than before.
My statement shows a different interest rate from the one I thought I was earning, which turned out to be an in-year rate change.

themes.name: the promotional rate expired with no reminder
themes.problem_statement: A promotional savings or card rate expires, the standard rate takes over automatically, and the customer only finds out afterwards.
themes.root_cause: Promotion end dates are not flagged in time and an expired offer cannot be extended or reapplied by the agent on the call.
examples: The 3% promotional rate on the savings account ended last month and the customer did not know what to do after the letter arrived.
I had seen a promotional higher rate for deposits of $50,000 or more, but it ended last week and the agent had no authority to match it.

themes.name: a limit or rule blocks the request and no exception exists
themes.problem_statement: A limit or rule - Regulation D, a daily check limit, a proof-of-address rule, a refund cap - blocks the request, with no exception route.
themes.root_cause: Limits and eligibility rules are applied uniformly and there is no documented exception process the front line can use.
examples: If there is not enough money to cover a payment there is a $35 NSF fee, it cannot be waived, and the only relief is a one business day grace period.
I asked to keep my existing accounts open alongside the new one and was told bank policy does not allow that.

themes.name: the call cuts off and nothing about the request is saved
themes.problem_statement: The call is cut off mid-request, so the customer rings back, verifies identity again and explains the whole request to a new agent.
themes.root_cause: Calls drop, often on transfer, and nothing about the interrupted request is saved, so the next agent starts from an empty screen.
examples: The customer had called earlier about the same question and the call was disconnected, so she had to start again with a new agent.
I had already spoken to an agent about this but the call got disconnected, so I had to call back and start again.

themes.name: this team cannot do it, so the customer places the next call
themes.problem_statement: After reaching an agent the customer is told the request belongs to another department or channel and is given a number to call, or a branch to visit, themselves.
themes.root_cause: Capability and authority are split across teams and channels with no warm handoff, so the customer has to place the next contact.
examples: The agent checked with a supervisor and told the customer to file a dispute claim through the disputes department, reached on option 3 of the customer service line.
I did not get the email confirmation of the direct debit that I usually receive, and this department could not look into it, so I have to call the e-banking line.

themes.name: after a transfer the ID and the story are taken again
themes.problem_statement: After a transfer the customer gives the same identity details and explains the same request again to the receiving department.
themes.root_cause: Case notes and verification status are not passed with the transfer, so the receiving team re-verifies and re-takes the story.
examples: After being transferred I had to give my account number, my ID and my utility bill all over again to the recovery department.
I was transferred to the fraud department and told I would need to give my account number and all the details again to them.

themes.name: phone verification fails because the details do not match
themes.problem_statement: The details the customer gives do not match the record, so the agent cannot act and refers them to fraud, verification or a branch.
themes.root_cause: Stale or mismatched identity and contact data on the account makes the standard phone verification script fail.
examples: The customer was unable to verify their identity with the initial agent when trying to change their signature on file, requiring a transfer to the fraud department.
The member number, name, date of birth and address did not match anything in the system, so the details had to be given and rechecked several times before verification worked.

themes.name: the first call gave no answer, so the customer calls back
themes.problem_statement: An earlier call about the same question ended without a resolution or a clear answer, so the customer calls back to follow it up.
themes.root_cause: No ownership or follow-up after the first contact, so unresolved requests come back as repeat calls.
examples: I am following up on the direct deposit issue I had yesterday, which is still not sorted out.
I called a few days ago about this account and did not get everything sorted, so I had to call back to finish it.

themes.name: Lost or stolen card blocked and replacement ordered
themes.problem_statement: A lost, stolen, compromised or expired card is blocked on the call and a replacement, sometimes a temporary card, is ordered with a delivery date given.
themes.root_cause: Front-line agents hold the rights to block a card and order a replacement, so the whole loss case closes in one contact.
examples: The agent offered a new card with a new PIN or a branch PIN reset; the customer asked for the card to be sent quickly because she has medical bills to pay.
My debit card expired last week and I needed a replacement sent to the address you already have on file.

themes.name: Misposted or duplicate transaction corrected on the call
themes.problem_statement: A wrongly posted, duplicated or unauthorised transaction is found on the call and corrected, reversed or raised as a dispute before the customer hangs up.
themes.root_cause: Agents can adjust and reverse postings and raise disputes directly, so the correction does not wait for a back-office queue.
examples: The agent restarted the $500 transfer on the call and said the funds should show in the account within the next hour.
While going through the transactions one had been posted for the wrong amount, and the agent corrected it on the call.

themes.name: Account change made and confirmed before the call ends
themes.problem_statement: Settings, standing instructions, contact details, products or the account itself are changed, opened or closed during the same call and read back.
themes.root_cause: The servicing tools sit on the front-line desktop with no second approval needed, so requests are actioned end to end in one call.
examples: I wanted text alerts when my balance falls below $1000 and when there is a transaction over $500.
The agent set up a weekly $50 automatic transfer from checking to savings with an email notification each time it runs.

themes.name: Requested document or item issued with a dated promise
themes.problem_statement: A statement, document, check, transfer, credential or piece of account information is produced, sent or confirmed during the call with a clear timeline.
themes.root_cause: Agents can trigger issuance and send documents from the call, so the customer leaves with the item or a dated promise.
examples: I asked for a stop payment on a $500 check and it was placed by the end of the call.
I needed a copy of last month's bank statement and asked for it to be emailed to me.

themes.name: Banker or advisor slot booked instead of a callback
themes.problem_statement: The customer is booked a named banker or advisor slot, or put straight through to an available specialist, instead of waiting for a callback.
themes.root_cause: Live visibility of banker availability from the phone desk lets the agent commit to a slot during the call.
examples: I called about financial planning because I want to start saving for retirement, and I was transferred to a planner who made a recommendation.
The customer asked for a banker's appointment to open a new account and was given one with a named banker within the next hour.

themes.name: other: helpful_staff
themes.problem_statement: Statements about helpful staff that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: verified another way when my usual details did not match
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot supply, or will not give, the usual identity details, and the agent works through alternative checks until one of them succeeds.
themes.root_cause: The standard verification script fits only one set of details, so agents improvise alternatives that are not part of the documented route.
examples: The phone number I gave did not match your records, so I had to be verified another way before anyone could help me.
I could not remember my account number, and the agent offered to verify me with my social security number instead.

themes.name: transferred to the specialist team that owns the request
themes.problem_statement: The agent cannot deal with the request themselves and connects the customer to the specialist department rather than leaving them to find it.
themes.root_cause: Ownership of specialised cases sits outside the front line, so the best the agent can do is a warm handoff to the right team.
examples: Was transferred to the customer service team to see whether any old statements or records could be retrieved another way.
My mother has checking, savings, investments and a small business loan with you and I want financial power of attorney in case she becomes incapacitated, which the legal department has to draft.

themes.name: alerts or extras added so the problem does not return
themes.problem_statement: Beyond the original request the agent sets up alerts, protections, tools or a better-fitting product so the same problem does not bring the customer back.
themes.root_cause: Agents can see the gap that caused the call and have the rights to close it, so they add the missing safeguard on the spot.
examples: I only had a checking account, so a savings account had to be opened before the standing order could be set up.
So she does not have to call to check her balance, the agent walked her through online banking, automatic payments and account alerts for low balances and large transactions.

themes.name: an alternative route when the request could not be done
themes.problem_statement: The requested action cannot be carried out, so the agent proposes and arranges a different route that gets the customer to the same outcome.
themes.root_cause: Hard product or timing limits block the literal request, and agents are left to find an alternative case by case.
examples: The bank offered a dispute form to investigate the erroneous $500 payment and potentially recover funds.
Wanted to stop payment on check number 1234 for $500 written to the wrong person, but the check had already been processed so a stop payment was no longer possible.

themes.name: a hardship plan or adviser arranged while I am struggling
themes.problem_statement: A customer in financial difficulty is given a payment plan, a counselling or adviser appointment, or is pointed to the support that already exists.
themes.root_cause: Hardship cases need options the agent cannot decide alone, so they are packaged into a plan or an appointment with someone who can.
examples: I lost my job, I am two months behind on my loan payments and behind on rent and bills, and I am worried I might lose my apartment.
The agent set up an appointment with a financial advisor for next Tuesday at 2 PM to go through the settlement options.

themes.name: other: clear_communication
themes.problem_statement: Statements about clear communication that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: had to call to find out what the account costs
themes.problem_statement: Fees, charges, minimum balances and the ways to waive them only become clear when an agent talks the customer through them, often on the customer's own figures.
themes.root_cause: Fee terms sit in schedules and letters written for compliance, so a customer cannot work out what an account costs without ringing.
examples: The customer was given the payoff calculation for her car loan: a $15,000 balance at 6% plus accrued interest and fees, for a total of $15,370.
The charity account has a $20 monthly maintenance fee and a 2.5% + $0.30 transaction fee per donation, with a possible non-profit discount to be checked.

themes.name: no way to compare rates and options without calling
themes.problem_statement: Rates, product features and the alternatives can only be put side by side by an agent, so the customer rings before choosing an account or a route.
themes.root_cause: There is no self-serve product comparison, so the trade-offs between products exist only on the agent's screens.
examples: I want to open a savings account and needed to know what interest rate I can expect and whether it is the best option for me.
The money market account pays 3.25% APY but needs a $1,000 minimum balance, and below that there is a $10 monthly maintenance fee and no interest.

themes.name: the limit or penalty only makes sense once explained
themes.problem_statement: A withdrawal limit, early-withdrawal penalty, notice period or joint liability rule only lands once an agent restates it and its consequences in plain words.
themes.root_cause: Product and regulatory rules reach the customer as legal wording, so the practical consequence is only learned by asking on a call.
examples: I did not know savings withdrawals are limited to six a month and wanted to know what happens if I need to withdraw more often.
The agent warned me that closing would affect the automatic payments and direct deposits on the account, which I will update myself.

themes.name: no single list of the documents and steps a request needs
themes.problem_statement: The customer has to call to learn which documents, steps, contacts and timeline a request needs, or risk a wasted trip or a rejected form.
themes.root_cause: Requirements are split across letters, forms and departments and published nowhere as one list, so only an agent can assemble them.
examples: Used a 2012 Honda Civic as collateral, the loan was paid off a few months ago, and he wants the title back.
Customer inquired about refinancing their car loan but was directed to a different department as the current department only handles personal loans.

themes.name: statement entries do not say where they came from
themes.problem_statement: An unrecognised charge, a pending or missing transaction or an odd balance cannot be explained from the statement, so the customer calls to have it traced and corrected.
themes.root_cause: Statement descriptions omit the source of an entry and the reason for a hold, so the posting detail behind it is visible only to an agent.
examples: A Chase Auto representative confirmed and helped delete a 'ghost' account incorrectly mapped to the customer's profile, describing it as a known systemic migration issue.
A $500 direct debit was supposed to come out yesterday and I wanted to confirm whether it had gone through.

themes.name: asked to prove who I am with no reason given
themes.problem_statement: The customer questions the identity check or cannot meet it, and only learns on the call why each detail is needed, how it is protected and what else is accepted.
themes.root_cause: Verification is demanded without stating the rule behind it or the accepted alternatives, so the request looks arbitrary until an agent explains it.
examples: Questioned why he has to provide his account number every time he calls when the bank should already have that information.
I asked why I have to provide identification every time I call when the bank already has all my information, and was told the law requires it on every call.

themes.name: what protects my money is not stated anywhere
themes.problem_statement: The customer calls to learn the deposit insurance limit, the security controls on the account or whether a suspicious email is genuine, and what to do next.
themes.root_cause: Deposit cover, security safeguards and scam warnings are not published where customers look, so they are only learned by asking on a call.
examples: I asked what my account is covered for and was told $250,000 of FDIC deposit insurance per depositor, per bank, across checking, savings, money market and CDs.
I wanted my account insurance coverage confirmed and was told it is $250,000 standard plus $250,000 optional, $500,000 in total.

themes.name: had to ring for a detail only the bank can see
themes.problem_statement: The customer needs a fact the bank holds - a routing number, the current balance, past transactions - and the phone is the only way to have it read back.
themes.root_cause: The detail is not shown where the customer looks, or online access is not set up, so a simple lookup turns into a call.
examples: The customer asked for his routing number to be confirmed; the agent verified the account number and confirmed the routing number on the call.
I was trying to confirm my routing number when the previous call got disconnected, and I need it confirmed.

themes.name: the ATM and branch locator could not find one for me
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot find an in-network ATM or a branch through the locator, and has to ring to be given the nearest address and directions to it.
themes.root_cause: The branch and ATM locator is hard to use or wrong about network coverage, so customers fall back to the phone for a location.
examples: I could not find an ATM in my network even though the bank promised that would be easy, so the agent found the nearest one and gave me directions.
I needed the closest ATM to 5th and Main and was given one at 6th and Elm, about a ten-minute walk, with directions.

themes.name: my credit score arrives with no reasons attached
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot tell why a score moved, or what closing a card or carrying a balance does, and learns the drivers and the levers only from an agent.
themes.root_cause: Bureau scores reach the customer as a number with no explanation, so the reasons and the actions that change them come only from reading the report on a call.
examples: Customer wants to know if closing credit card accounts would help or hurt his credit score.
Hesitated over every option because of not wanting to be stuck with debt, and only agreed after the agent explained credit is built through regular on-time payments.

themes.name: my rate is higher than the one I was advertised
themes.problem_statement: The rate charged is above the advertised, signed-up or promotional rate, and the customer calls to learn how the APR was priced and when the promotion ended.
themes.root_cause: Advertised rates are ranges and promotional rates expire, but the personalised price and the end date appear only in letters and fine print.
examples: The customer called to understand the Annual Percentage Rate (APR) on their credit card and inquired about the reasons for its 22.99% rate.
The customer is confused why their Annual Percentage Rate (APR) is 18.99% when they believed their interest rate was 12%, requesting an explanation for the difference.

themes.name: the merger notice does not say what happens to my account
themes.problem_statement: After a merger announcement the customer must call to learn what happens to their accounts, cards and rates, and whether they have to do anything themselves.
themes.root_cause: Merger notices describe the deal but not its effect on an individual account, leaving the phone as the only place to confirm it.
examples: As a long-time customer I was worried what the merger with First National Bank means for my accounts, and was told they stay here with the same services and features.
Customer asks how the merger with First National Bank will affect their account and what actions, if any, they need to take.

themes.name: the bank's community and green programmes are hard to find
themes.problem_statement: The customer calls to learn what the bank funds, matches or runs - donation matching, volunteering, mentoring, renewable investment - and what the figures are.
themes.root_cause: Community and environmental commitments are not published where customers look, so the programmes and their numbers only reach them on a call.
examples: Donations to eligible charities are matched up to $500 a year per customer, with the full list published under the Community tab on the website.
I want to get involved in my community and needed to hear what programs the bank runs; the youth mentorship programme was the one that interested me.

themes.name: I cannot find the function I need in online banking
themes.problem_statement: The customer cannot locate or work a feature in online banking - bill pay, transfers, privacy or email preferences - and needs an agent to walk the screens with them.
themes.root_cause: Self-service screens are not discoverable and some settings only the customer can change, so the agent has to navigate them click by click.
examples: The agent showed me where the Bill Pay and Transfer Funds tabs are in online banking and how to add payees and move money.
After being asked to try another browser or clear the cache, the customer used Chrome and the address update worked.

themes.name: a rule change letter that does not say what changes for me
themes.problem_statement: A notice about a regulation or tariff change gives no detail, so the customer calls to learn the extra paperwork, the higher costs and the options left to them.
themes.root_cause: Regulatory change notices state the rule but never its effect on an individual customer or business, so the translation only happens on a call.
examples: A letter said new regulations had been implemented but gave little detail, so the customer called to find out what they mean for the account.
I import goods and cannot work out what the new tariffs will do to my bottom line; the agent explained they are taxes on imports and suggested other suppliers, negotiating, or passing costs on.

themes.name: what the advice service covers is published nowhere
themes.problem_statement: A customer unsure whether they are on track for a goal has to call to learn what the planning or advisory service covers, what it costs and how to book a meeting.
themes.root_cause: The advisory offering's scope, price and booking route are not described where customers look, so they are only set out on the call.
examples: Asked what the new investment services involve and how to meet an advisor, saying he is not very knowledgeable about investing.
I am approaching retirement with some savings set aside and do not know whether it is enough to retire comfortably.

themes.name: only on the call do I learn the bank will not do this
themes.problem_statement: The customer asks for tax or investment advice, a donation or research the bank does not provide, and only hears on the call that it is out of scope, with an outside route.
themes.root_cause: The limits of the bank's service, and who does it instead, are not published anywhere, so a refusal is only discovered after asking.
examples: The customer asked about tax implications and was told bond interest is generally taxable income and that the bank does not give tax advice.
The bank's cryptocurrency services do not provide detailed market trends or investment advice, requiring the customer to seek external information.

themes.name: the referral offer's conditions are not in the advert
themes.problem_statement: The customer wants to use a referral offer but has to call to learn what it pays, what the person referred must do and when the credit actually lands.
themes.root_cause: Referral offers are advertised as a headline amount, leaving the qualifying steps and the payment timing to be spelled out by an agent.
examples: Customer called to inquire about referral program benefits and how to refer someone, understanding that she could get a $50 credit towards her next loan payment.
